title: Scribe-Adjusted EBITDA: Privileged Diligence for Physician Deals
one_liner: A fixed-price, 10-business-day, counsel-engaged report that tells private equity buyers how much of a scribe-enabled physician group's revenue is real, and what the rest could cost them.
lineage: mutation of I0389 ('Independent Auditor for AI-Scribed Billing'), type: sharpened
cluster: Proving AI controls and human review to insurers, auditors and clients

judges.fatal_flaw: Transient diligence item; incumbents like VMG can copy within a quarter
judges.note: Fixed-price report protects millions of deal value, clean control-group design, buyer already pays for diligence. Services-shaped, VMG could copy; scribe uplift may fade.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: $30k report protects ~$8M of deal price, sold through deal counsel, 80% margin. Timely and original. Trust barrier for a new shop; VMG could copy.

judges.fatal_flaw: VMG Health can copy fast; depends on data-room claims access.
judges.note: New diligence line item. Staggered scribe rollouts give each target a built-in control group, and a $30k report protects roughly $8M of price. Fast PE buyer path.

title: Home Equity Assurance for Data Center Neighbors
one_liner: A neutral calculation agent runs a county-approved, developer-funded home-value guarantee for houses near proposed data centers, using pre-announcement baselines and public sale records with no sensors, and unspent escrow reverts to the developer, which makes it cheaper than $10k checks and more credible.
lineage: mutation of I1172 ('Neutral Baselines and Neighbor Guarantees for Data Centers'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Localities, utilities and landowners facing speculative data-center demand

judges.fatal_flaw: Payout structure may be regulated as insurance; developer counsel may balk at admission.
judges.note: Developers burned by 'bribe' checks; guarantee is cheaper and more credible; county-embedded neutral agent earns escrow and per-home fees.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow developer and county sales cycle; insurance-law classification risk before first revenue.
judges.note: Original; funds from developer budget already spent on bribe-style checks; formula trigger avoids causation fights; one pilot is worth about $1M.

judges.fatal_flaw: Developer counsel may resist pre-committed payouts; insurance-law classification; slow county sales.
judges.note: Right insight: a formula-triggered value guarantee beats $10k checks. Huge 2026 data-center backlash and a wind-farm precedent. Large per-program revenue, but slower to close.

title: Auto Loan-End Event Exchange for Add-On Refunds
one_liner: Start by recovering unearned add-on refunds on repossessed and charged-off loans for small lenders on pure contingency (cash the lender itself keeps), then turn those lender-attested loan-end events into a neutral exchange that administrators, carriers and regulators plug into, so refunds become a statutory event pushed to the administrator instead of a claim the borrower must pull.
lineage: mutation of I0109 ('Payoff-Triggered Refund Recovery for Credit Unions'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Unclaimed money: settlements, refunds, penalties and unpaid invoices

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Information gap (nobody tells the administrator the loan ended) plus contingency pricing gives low-friction entry; the loan-end event dataset is a real exchange asset.

judges.fatal_flaw: Exchange stage needs administrator cooperation; stage 1 is only contingency recovery services.
judges.note: Real cash on repos, lender-paid contingency, sellable in six months, with an escape from recovery-vendor commodity into an event exchange and early-termination data.

judges.fatal_flaw: Administrators stall; small-lender repo volume modest; exchange layer speculative.
judges.note: Pure-contingency repo refund recovery is the lender's own cash, no integration, no budget fight. Stage 1 is sellable; exchange is bloat.

title: ERCOT Large-Load Energization Files, Fixed Fee
one_liner: A two-engineer Texas specialist that sells neocloud and colo developers a fixed-fee, six-week package of ISO-acceptable PSS/E and EMT models, a ride-through study and a compliance file, with a fee kicker paid when ERCOT accepts it.
lineage: mutation of I0996 ('Grid-Code Models for AI Data Centers'), type: sharpened
cluster: Getting power for large loads and storage

judges.fatal_flaw: ERCOT may accept self-attestation, collapsing the acceptance-kicker premise.
judges.note: Regulation-forced demand, eight-figure cost of delay, fixed fee, single-regulator focus. Reusable models plus ISO precedent can expand to PJM and MISO.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Selling regulator acceptance, not models, in a fresh rule window with reusable HIL-validated platform models; needs scarce power-electronics talent and OEM NDAs.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Acute, budgeted pain: energization delay costs millions versus a $150k fee. Narrow ERCOT focus builds acceptance know-how. Must confirm ERCOT requires more than self-attestation.

title: Finish Crew: Stranded Solar Job Completion
one_liner: A completion contractor that takes half-built solar jobs abandoned by bankrupt installers all the way to permission-to-operate, and is paid by the lenders whose loans go bad while the system sits dark.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Residential solar leftovers: orphaned systems, leases and liens

judges.fatal_flaw: First-wave jobs already assigned; crews, licensing and working capital strain a scrappy team.
judges.note: Urgent lender pain, concrete named buyers, event-driven; forensic-records wedge sells without crews; legacy books and servicers uncontested.

judges.fatal_flaw: State contractor licensing and lenders' existing in-house step-in crews may shrink the buyer pool.
judges.note: Stranded solar is a records and legal-standing problem, not labor. Lender pays, hard Freedom Forever clock, tens of thousands of dark systems. Strongest why-now and buyer.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs licensed crews across states; event-driven, lumpy demand; first wave likely allocated.
judges.note: Records-first insight and lender-as-buyer are sharp, and legacy stranded books (Titan, SunPower, Sunnova) are large.

title: Independent Auditor for AI-Scribed Billing
one_liner: A continuous, coder-signed check on whether ambient AI scribe notes actually support the E/M levels being billed, before the payers or the government find out.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Proving AI controls and human review to insurers, auditors and clients

judges.fatal_flaw: Incumbent audit firms can rebrand identical coder review within a quarter.
judges.note: Independent audit of the scribe wave, with False Claims Act pull. Free claims-only hook gets fast first customers; defensibility is thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: VMG, MDaudit, Healthicity can replicate within a quarter; no technical moat.
judges.note: Real payer downcoding and FCA pressure; free claims-only diagnostic is a cheap hook. Incumbent audit firms can rebrand fast; PHI and BAAs slow sales.

judges.fatal_flaw: Incumbents (VMG, MDaudit, Healthicity) can rebrand the same claims analysis within a quarter.
judges.note: Right insight: scribe risk is MDM and time statements, not HPI bloat. Huge prize, live FCA and downcoding pressure, a free diagnostic as the wedge.

title: Line-Keyed Cross-Examination Kits for LOP Defense
one_liner: A $395, 48-hour kit for defense counsel that turns a letter-of-protection bill into line-by-line cross-examination questions and a signed rebuttal, with the testifying coder as the real profit center.
lineage: mutation of I0428 ('Coder-Signed Reasonable-Value Reports for Injury Defense'), type: sharpened
cluster: Small litigation practices lacking evidence, records and benchmark tools

judges.fatal_flaw: Human coder labor and testimony cap scalability; carrier vendors could add flat-fee reviews.
judges.note: Concrete, cheap-to-start counsel-facing wedge priced under pre-approval thresholds; testifying-coder track record compounds. Services-heavy, so prize is moderate.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: $395 kit priced under expert pre-approval threshold, 80%+ margin, testifying coder is real moat. Reachable defense boutiques; hot LOP fight in TX/GA.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Priced under carrier pre-approval, with human-signed testimony as the margin. Fast to test, huge LOP litigation pool, and it escapes EvenUp and FAIR Health.

title: Cattle Lien Registry and Sale-Barn Exit Alerts
one_liner: Invert the problem: instead of counting cattle in the pasture, watch the few gates cattle must leave through. Start with consignment alerts to lenders and lien matching for auction markets, then grow into the neutral title registry for cattle.
lineage: mutation of I0338 ('Chute-Side Cow Counts for Ag Lenders'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Lenders and investors unable to verify collateral exists

judges.fatal_flaw: Two-sided cold start; borrowers can sell privately, bypassing barns and the alerts.
judges.note: Watching cattle exits is a sharp, uncrowded insight; October calf run enables an immediate pilot; lender pledge data is a real cornered resource.

judges.fatal_flaw: Barns may refuse sharing consignor data; consignors flee markets that report them.
judges.note: Concrete manual pilot this fall: consignment lists matched to lender loans; barns have liability motive; lender pledge data becomes cornered resource.

judges.fatal_flaw: Barns may refuse to share consignor lists; two-sided cold start.
judges.note: 'Fraud needs an exit' is a right and non-obvious inversion. Record cattle prices, peak calf run now, and lender-funded pledge data is a cornered resource.

title: Herd Roll-Forward: Lender-Paid Cattle Collateral Reconciliation
one_liner: Sell ag lenders a loan covenant that rebuilds the borrower's herd from paper that third parties generated (vet records, sale-barn settlements, brand certificates, tag and vaccine purchases) and flags loans where expected head and claimed head do not reconcile.
lineage: mutation of I0338 ('Chute-Side Cow Counts for Ag Lenders'), type: sharpened
cluster: Lenders and investors unable to verify collateral exists

judges.fatal_flaw: Paper-reconciliation labor per loan; needs vets, barns and brand agencies to release records.
judges.note: Information-rights rider fixes adverse selection; lender-paid per-loan fee; fraud fear is budgeted; conservative ag banks slow but pilot is cheap.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow bank adoption; borrower rider and third-party record access may be contested.
judges.note: Count the paper, not cattle: covenant-funded reconciliation from third-party records fixes adverse selection; record cattle prices and fraud losses give lenders budget and urgency.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Count the paper, not cattle: lender-paid, covenant-based, fixes parent's adverse selection. Credible collateral-audit automation; moderate prize, slow bank sales, possible record gaps.

title: Lender-Required Curtailment Reports for Data Centers
one_liner: An independent, productized report, like a Phase I environmental report but for power, that tells data center lenders how many hours a campus can legally run its generators when the grid curtails it.
lineage: mutation of I0836 ('Air-Permit Unlock for Idle Data Center Diesel'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Getting power for large loads and storage

judges.fatal_flaw: Lenders may never make it a closing condition; independent engineers can copy it.
judges.note: Sharp non-consensus insight (generator hour caps) sold as a Phase-I-style gating report to a buyer with money; cheap to build, lender-paid.

judges.fatal_flaw: No lender requires it; a closing-condition standard takes years to establish.
judges.note: Sharp insight: legal 100-hour cap makes assumed generator cover illusory. But no lender mandates this report yet; you must create the closing-condition standard first.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lenders may not demand it at closing; independent engineers can bolt it on.
judges.note: Contrarian: the diesel fallback everyone assumes is capped by permit hours. Real 2026 PJM/SB6 shift, lender budgets, cheap to prove with public permits.

title: Smoke Report Autopsy for Policyholder Advocates
one_liner: An adequacy auditor that scores any carrier-side smoke, ash and soot report against a public, versioned sampling grid. It then drafts the AB 1795 deficiency letter and supplemental sampling plan, and sells to public adjusters and plaintiff attorneys in the Eaton and Palisades zones.
lineage: mutation of I0715 ('Interim Smoke-Damage Protocol Before the State Standard'), type: sharpened
cluster: Flood and fire survivors: mapping, buyouts, claims and rebuilding

judges.fatal_flaw: Wedge tied to one disaster; CIH second opinions substitute; year-one revenue about $2M.
judges.note: Acute, dated pain with a hard statutory hook (AB 1795) and fast paid audits. Sampling-pattern dataset is the asset; it could generalize to other claim reports.

judges.fatal_flaw: Event-driven niche; capped when state standards land; needs CIH partner.
judges.note: Concentrated LA buyers, urgent deadlines, claim-funded budgets and an AB 1795 clock; ten public adjusters closable fast; dataset is the asset.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small market, capped when DTSC standards arrive; licensure questions on plan drafting.
judges.note: Omission-list audit is sharp, with a hard 1/1/2027 forcing date and buyers reachable in weeks. Sells no sampling, so it avoids the conflicted incumbents.

title: Cure Desk: Cash-Worker Packets for Health Centers
one_liner: A Spanish-first text-message case tool for health-center enrollment staff that turns a Medicaid noncompliance notice (or a pre-emptive look-back audit) into a state-formatted evidence packet for cash-paid workers, built on batch attestations from the crew leaders, landlords and households who pay them, billed per accepted packet.
lineage: mutation of I0573 ('Medicaid Hours Wallet for Gig Workers'), type: sharpened
cluster: Benefit-rule changes: Medicaid work rules, SNAP and ACA cliffs

judges.fatal_flaw: Demand timing depends on states ending self-attestation; health centers are thin-margin payers.
judges.note: Hard dated trigger, cash-worker residue unserved by bank-link vendors, attester network compounds; per-case pricing fits health-center budgets.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Fixes parent: per-packet billing to health centers, serves cash workers bank-linking cannot reach, attester network compounds. Revenue may ramp late if self-attestation lingers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Self-attestation through 2027 delays urgency; health centers lack a budget line.
judges.note: Attester-rail network effect for cash workers is genuinely non-obvious; Medicaid work rules start Jan 2027, timing fits a 6-month first customer. Payer weakness is the risk.

title: China-Asset Diligence Desk for Pharma BD
one_liner: A bilingual scientist-plus-software sprint that verifies China-sourced drug packages (raw data, GLP and CMC standing, ownership chain) in 72 hours for US buyers.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Biotech capital: diligence and salvage

judges.fatal_flaw: Seller data-export rules may block raw-data access; 72-hour promise unrealistic.
judges.note: Record China licensing flow, thin bilingual diligence bench, buyers who pay $25-70k easily. Moat is scientist judgment and trust, not software.

judges.fatal_flaw: Seller data-room access and China data-export rules may block raw-data review; 72-hour promise.
judges.note: Record China in-licensing flow, $25-70k tickets, reachable NewCo VCs and mid-caps, strong why-now. Trust and scientist judgment is the moat. Best ticket-to-effort ratio in batch.

judges.fatal_flaw: Seller raw-data access blocked by Chinese export rules; 72-hour promise unrealistic.
judges.note: Real BIOSECURE and China-licensing catalyst, and tacit-standards diligence is a genuine gap. But big pharma has in-house benches and the moat is only people and trust.

title: Independent Referee for Survey Panel Data
one_liner: An audit that tells research buyers what share of their online-panel responses came from bots, agents or fraud farms, and recalibrates the study against a verified-human control sample.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Gatekeepers drowning in AI-generated submissions and bot responses

judges.fatal_flaw: Building the verified-human control panel is slow and costly; detection rivals are funded.
judges.note: AI agents breaking panels is a live crisis; verified-human control sample is a real cornered asset; referee neutrality is the non-consensus angle.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs verified-human control panel; building or licensing one is slow and costly.
judges.note: Buyer-side referee with ground-truth humans is genuinely non-obvious as agents defeat attention checks; calibration, not detection, is the gap. Vendors cannot referee themselves.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Panel fraud is urgent and the control-sample calibration is novel. Detection is crowded, and the address-recruited human panel is slow and costly to build.

title: Fixed-Price Guaranteed Clearance of Unknown Lead Lines
one_liner: Take the whole unknown-lines problem at a fixed price per line with an acceptance guarantee, and make money by routing each line to the cheapest method that will satisfy the state (records mining, meter-swap photos, paid photos, probe, pothole).
lineage: mutation of I0463 ('Pay Home Inspectors to Find Lead Pipes'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Small water utilities: staffing, revenue leakage, lead lines and nitrate

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs working capital and a state-accepted method before guarantee is safe to sell.
judges.note: Deadline-driven, SRF-funded pain; outcome pricing plus a router over competitors-as-suppliers is a real margin spread. Municipal sales cycles slow first revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Acceptance-guarantee risk and working capital; engineering firms and state rules can undercut.
judges.note: Outcome-priced router across cheaper methods is sharp counter-positioning in a huge, funded mandate. Services-heavy and government-slow, in a crowded lead-line field.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs working capital and state acceptance of non-physical verification; guarantee risk.
judges.note: Outcome pricing with a cost-ladder router has a big prize and real vision-model why-now. Insight is less novel, and the guarantee strains a scrappy team.

title: Phantom Pipeline Audits for Utility Rate-Case Intervenors
one_liner: Sell to the ratepayers who pay for phantom load, meaning industrial customer groups and state consumer advocates in IRP, CPCN and large-load-tariff dockets, a testimony-ready audit of how much of a utility's confidential data-center pipeline is physically real.
lineage: mutation of I0079 ('Phantom Load Vetting Desk for Rural Utilities'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Localities, utilities and landowners facing speculative data-center demand

judges.fatal_flaw: Intervenors' econometric experts may suffice; consumer advocates have thin budgets.
judges.note: Adversarial phantom-load audit sold into live dockets. Docket calendar forces deadlines, 2026 affordability politics, conflicted rivals, cross-utility duplicate view. Real shift, no procurement cycle.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Docket deadlines set urgency, intervenors already have counsel and expert budgets, $40-120k tickets. Adversarial position is structurally clean. Risk is outsider visibility into anonymized pipeline entries.

judges.fatal_flaw: Expert-witness consulting with few dockets; econometric experts may already suffice.
judges.note: Adversarial positioning with a real budget and docket deadlines. Services business; the Phantom Ratio Index for funds is the only venture path.

title: Satellite Witness for Neighbor Construction Claims
one_liner: A fixed-price, court-ready satellite-radar history of a condo tower's movement before and during the neighbor's pile-driving, sold through the plaintiff-side attorneys who represent Miami-Dade condo associations.
lineage: mutation of I1289 ('Settlement Passports for Florida High-Rise Condos'), type: sharpened
cluster: Novel environmental and infrastructure data from satellites and crowd-sensing

judges.fatal_flaw: Sentinel-1 revisit cannot capture vibration cracks; Daubert challenge likely; roughly $600K year-one ceiling.
judges.note: Retroactive satellite baseline at moment of peak willingness to pay is smart; attorney channel is real, but Miami-only and InSAR cannot see vibration.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Live trigger, adversary and budget; attorneys advance costs; retroactive baseline sensors cannot match; free data. Small Miami niche, method copyable, Daubert needs credible expert.

judges.fatal_flaw: Open method means no moat; small plaintiff-attorney buyer pool.
judges.note: Retroactive satellite baseline sold at peak dispute urgency is a clever inversion. Live permit triggers, near-free data, a reproducibility story, fast first sales.

title: Independent Collateral Verifier for Warehouse Lenders
one_liner: Sell the same listing-vs-ledger signal not to the floorplan lender but to the lender's lender: credit funds and banks that fund floorplan and subprime auto lenders and get a borrower-supplied VIN tape they have never been able to check, delivered as a signed monthly verification certificate that borrowers pay for through facility fees.
lineage: mutation of I0218 ('Sold-Out-of-Trust Radar for Floorplan Lenders'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Lenders and investors unable to verify collateral exists

judges.fatal_flaw: Listing-vanish signal works for inventory floorplan, not subprime loan collateral; niche is small.
judges.note: Strong post-Tricolor why-now and sticky facility-fee structure; independence is the product. Credit-fund sales cycles long, so only 1-3 paying facilities by month six.

judges.fatal_flaw: Listing-vanish signal is noisy and misses Tricolor-style double-pledged loan collateral.
judges.note: Selling verification to the lender's lender, paid via facility fees, is a smart payer inversion after Tricolor; sticky covenant revenue if the signal proves precise.

judges.fatal_flaw: Listing-vanish signal fits floorplan inventory, not retail subprime collateral; noisy.
judges.note: Sells to the lender's lender, fee written into facility docs, post-Tricolor timing, sticky and generalizable to any borrowing-base tape.

title: Lead Line Photos Taken During Meter Swaps
one_liner: Add a 90-second, three-photo service-entry protocol with on-device AI to the water-meter change-out crews a utility already sends into basements, and sell it to the utility as a $10-14 per line change order.
lineage: mutation of I0463 ('Pay Home Inspectors to Find Lead Pipes'), type: sharpened
cluster: Small water utilities: staffing, revenue leakage, lead lines and nitrate

judges.fatal_flaw: Meter contractors may already be mobilized; state may reject contractor photos.
judges.note: Borrows tariff-mandated meter access to reach absentee-owner lines no portal can. Non-obvious, funded by AMI wave and lead deadlines, large per-line prize, change-order sale.

judges.fatal_flaw: State rules may not accept contractor photos to reclassify unknown lines.
judges.note: Piggybacks funded meter swaps and tariff-backed access, fixing parent's supply, evidence and liability problems; meter vendors could copy.

judges.fatal_flaw: States may reject contractor photos as evidence; meter installers could build it themselves.
judges.note: Rides an already-funded crew trip, a clever access hack with a real deadline. Utility procurement is slow; state acceptance of contractor photos unproven.

title: Work-Permit Gap Desk for Frontline Employers
one_liner: Employer-paid, pre-cliff delay suits for workers whose EAD renewals are pending, sold to home-care, nursing and staffing employers as a per-worker maintenance plan instead of a one-off legal purchase.
lineage: mutation of I1062 ('Delay-Suit Rails for Stuck Immigration Cases'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Immigrant households and workers: status deadlines and paperwork

judges.fatal_flaw: Employer-paid delay suits face ethics, discrimination and shifting immigration-policy risk.
judges.note: Moving the payer to the employer turns lumpy legal spend into a forecastable subscription. Real cliff, proven remedy, but politically and ethically exposed.

judges.fatal_flaw: Policy shifts or hostile districts could erode mandamus success.
judges.note: Employer feels lost-worker cost now, expiry dates forecastable, flat-fee suits via panel attorneys. Recurring plus per-case revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Employer-paid delay suits carry ethics and discrimination exposure; mandamus win rates uneven.
judges.note: Employer as payer turns lumpy legal buys into a forecastable renewal calendar. EAD auto-extension ended Oct 2025, big frontline workforce. Legal-structure risk is real.

title: Unit Tests for Benefit Law: Eligibility System Conformance
one_liner: Invert the drill: aim the same synthetic households and adjudicated answer keys at the eligibility software itself, selling H.R.1 conformance test packs to states and system vendors, with an aim to become the standard test suite that state RFPs cite.
lineage: mutation of I1240 ('Flight simulator drills for county SNAP eligibility workers'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Benefit-rule changes: Medicaid work rules, SNAP and ACA cliffs

judges.fatal_flaw: State UAT procurement and answer-key adjudication need scarce experts before first revenue.
judges.note: H.R.1 reprogramming deadline creates funded, urgent demand; independent state-signed answer keys are a real asset. Government sales still slow to first check.

judges.fatal_flaw: State procurement is slow; vendors and IV&V incumbents may block independent answer keys.
judges.note: Hard 2026 forcing function (H.R.1 reprogramming, error-rate cliff); testing the machine not the worker is non-obvious; state-signed answer keys compound into a citeable standard.

judges.fatal_flaw: State procurement outlasts the H.R.1 window; nonprofits like PolicyEngine can give it away.
judges.note: Independent state-signed answer keys, UL-for-eligibility, is original with a hard deadline; slow government sales and free rivals threaten it.

title: Holdout Ledger: Landowner-Side Assembly Intelligence
one_liner: The landowner's half of the courthouse tape. It shows farm families and heirs in an assembly corridor who is buying around them, how close the buyer is to finishing, and how much leverage the last holdouts have, paid on closing.
lineage: mutation of I0773 ('Courthouse Tape: Land-Assembly Radar for Infrastructure'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Land and property facts trapped in county records

judges.fatal_flaw: Unproven that developers record option memoranda pre-announcement; county recorder bulk access uncertain.
judges.note: Counter-positioned against every data vendor; contingent fee on multi-million land deals; data-center land rush gives urgent demand and clear ROI.

judges.fatal_flaw: Broker licensing, lawyer fee-split rules and developer retaliation; options may be unrecorded.
judges.note: Genuinely counter-positioned: landowners are the unserved counterparty and a $199 report sells directly by mail. Fee-sharing, licensing and NDA-interference exposure is dangerous.

judges.fatal_flaw: Unproven that options are recorded early; broker licensing and fee-splitting rules bite.
judges.note: Counter-positioned: every data vendor sells to developers, none to landowners facing $100k/acre offers. Stakes justify paying. Legal structure and recording premise are the risks.

title: A Price Reporting Agency for Trade Materials
one_liner: Turn pooled supply-house invoices into contract-grade, SKU-level price evidence for the trades, starting with cost-change certificates that win price-adjustment change orders and ending as the index that escalation clauses and price-lock guarantees reference.
lineage: mutation of I0068 ('Contingency Audit of Unbilled Plumbing Materials'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Small trade and service firms underpricing and leaking margin

judges.fatal_flaw: Chicken-and-egg: certificates from one shop's invoices carry little weight before an index exists.
judges.note: Becoming the named reference in contracts is the durable PRA moat; tariff-driven escalation disputes give a dated pain and a certificate wedge.

judges.fatal_flaw: Certificates are tiny tickets; counterparties may not accept a vendor as contract-grade reference.
judges.note: Pain is real and certificates start with one shop's invoices. The PRA end-state is a decade-long network play; early revenue is small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Counterparties must accept an unproven index; supply houses and antitrust concerns push back.
judges.note: Largest ceiling in the batch: the named contract reference in tariff-driven escalation disputes. Certificate wedge needs no network and earns first revenue.

title: Ruling-Backed Tariff Engineering for Product Brands
one_liner: A productized design-and-ruling service that helps mid-market brands legitimately re-spec products across tariff-line boundaries and locks the result in with a CBP binding ruling.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Tariff cost, classification and customs for small importers

judges.fatal_flaw: Tariff rule changes or later 232 listing can erase redesign savings overnight.
judges.note: Real pain, fast-paying audits, but volatile tariff regime, rulings bind only the addressee, and brokers or trade lawyers can copy a services model.

judges.fatal_flaw: Rulings bind only addressee and identical goods; Section 232 list changes can undo redesigns.
judges.note: Design-stage tariff engineering plus binding rulings is a real, unpackaged mid-market gap with large rate spreads and fast fixed-fee cash.

judges.fatal_flaw: Ruling delays and 232 list changes can erase redesign savings; liability if advice wrong.
judges.note: Huge, budgeted tariff pain; $4.5K audit sells fast to thousands of mid-market brands; ruling filing and counsel review add durable margin. Services-first, low capital.

title: Flight simulator drills for county SNAP eligibility workers
one_liner: Short daily drills using synthetic cases built from the state's own error taxonomy, sold to county social-services directors who are about to pay for every eligibility mistake.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Benefit-rule changes: Medicaid work rules, SNAP and ACA cliffs

judges.fatal_flaw: States own training budgets; county sales slow; per-state case libraries are costly.
judges.note: Hard two-year H.R.1 deadline with dollar penalties. Synthetic cases dodge the PII barrier, and Medicaid work-requirement training is an obvious bigger adjacent market.

judges.fatal_flaw: States own training; county budgets thin; per-state case libraries costly to maintain.
judges.note: Hard H.R.1 clock, buyers in pain now, and synthetic cases dodge PII and security review so selling starts in weeks. Govtech speed is the risk.

judges.fatal_flaw: States own eligibility training; per-state case libraries costly; county budgets thin.
judges.note: Hard two-year clock and PII-free synthetic cases speed selling. But buyer is really the state, and Maximus or the state LMS vendor can bolt on.

title: The Pharmacy-Verified Reimbursement Index
one_liner: A furnisher-funded bureau, like a credit bureau for PBM payments, that turns what pharmacies actually pay and are actually paid into a reference index that state laws, Medicaid rate-setting and transparent-PBM contracts can cite, launching with a per-state Underwater Index sold to pharmacy associations for the 2027 legislative sessions.
lineage: mutation of I1266 ('Pharmacy-Side PBM Ledger for Employers'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Independent pharmacies squeezed by PBMs, refund floats and deserts

judges.fatal_flaw: Pooled reimbursement data risks antitrust and PBM confidentiality objections; legitimacy takes years.
judges.note: Index-as-standard play: pharmacy remits are the only paid-versus-cost ground truth; associations fund first state reports for 2027 sessions.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs antitrust-safe data pooling and PBM-confidentiality clearance before any index is credible.
judges.note: Biggest prize here: neutral standard cited by statute and contracts. Association-funded evidence pack is sellable by December, but data network is slow to build.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs critical mass of contributing pharmacies; antitrust and PBM-contract confidentiality exposure.
judges.note: Neutral index cited in statutes is a standards play timed to 2027 sessions; association evidence packs give early cash, but data cold-start is slow.

title: Serial Match: AP-Only Recovery for Exchange Buyers
one_liner: A success-fee audit that takes one accounts-payable export from an independent rotable pool or Part 145 station, finds money its repair vendors already owe, and collects it. It starts with credits the vendor has already conceded, then moves to repeat-failure claims.
lineage: mutation of I0195 ('Contingency Recovery of Missed Rotable Repair Warranties'), type: sharpened
cluster: Warranty claims left unfiled

judges.fatal_flaw: Few hundred qualifying pools; short warranty windows may yield under 1% recovery.
judges.note: Contingency audit with sequenced zero-dispute first pass is smart and fast to cash, but small buyer universe and thin evidence of recoverable dollars.

judges.fatal_flaw: Pool segment is small; short warranty windows may keep yield under 1%.
judges.note: Contingency fee, conceded credits first, free scan, first cash in weeks. Clear small-back-office buyer, real dollars, explicit kill test.

judges.fatal_flaw: Credits owed may be small; no proof vendors concede claims; assumptions unverified.
judges.note: Contingency audit starting with already-conceded credits gives cash in weeks with no dispute. Practical and feasible; insight is a vertical transplant of freight audit.

title: Hall-Ready Gate for Liquid-Cooled GPU Tranches
one_liner: A fixed-price, 10-business-day release/hold decision, made 60-90 days before GPU delivery, on whether a liquid-cooled data hall will be energized and flowing when the racks arrive.
lineage: mutation of I0365 ('Ground-Truth Diligence for GPU-Backed Lenders'), type: sharpened
cluster: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: People-bound consultancy; incumbent independent engineers can add this service line easily.
judges.note: Option-trigger framing and the rider access mechanism are clever, and credit desks can pay fast. Ceiling is small and moat only accrues after 30 gates.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Fixed-price release/hold decision at the moment of billion-dollar exposure; $30K is noise to lenders. Cx bench hireable; buyer pool small but reachable via law-firm rider.

judges.fatal_flaw: People-bound service on scarce Cx engineers; incumbent IEs can add it; site access uncertain.
judges.note: Option-trigger framing and Readiness Rider access trick are smart. But it rides the consensus AI-capex story and has no software moat.

title: Independent Post-Reform Valuation for Medical Lien Funders
one_liner: A neutral, coder-signed valuation agent that tells LOP factoring companies and the lenders behind them what their medical receivables are worth after tort reform.
lineage: mutation of I0428 ('Coder-Signed Reasonable-Value Reports for Injury Defense'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Small litigation practices lacking evidence, records and benchmark tools

judges.fatal_flaw: Target market shrinking under tort reform; funders secretive; few buyers.
judges.note: Lender-appointed valuation agent with proprietary collection data is a smart conflict fix. Private credit entering medical receivables gives a real forcing party, but a small customer pool.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Fresh customer set with no vendor aimed at it and high ACV via lender-driven valuation. But niche of 30-40 funders, and lender mandate is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few, secretive funders may withhold data or refuse to pay for valuation.
judges.note: Treating LOP bills as collateral, with the lender as appointing party, is a sharp inversion. Post-reform cohort resolving now; realized-collection data is a real moat.

title: Site-Control Check for Utility Large-Load Queues
one_liner: A neutral 48-hour report on whether each large-load applicant really controls the land it names, sold to the utilities that must now screen speculative data center requests and billed through to the applicants.
lineage: mutation of I0773 ('Courthouse Tape: Land-Assembly Radar for Infrastructure'), type: sharpened
cluster: Land and property facts trapped in county records

judges.fatal_flaw: Utility procurement is slow and county recorder access is uneven
judges.note: Utility-side neutral, forced demand from SB 6, applicant-paid pass-through, cross-utility parcel index moat. Modest direct ARR but real standard potential.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow utility procurement; applicants already supply site-control documents utilities can check cheaply.
judges.note: Utility-compelled parcel list makes verification easy; free retrospective audit is a smart hook. Utilities can use counsel or landmen instead; $2K reports are thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: SB 6 collateral and site-control mandates make applicants self-prove, shrinking need.
judges.note: Utility-side neutral with a cross-utility duplicate-parcel index is a real network effect. Sharper than the Phantom Load Desk, but exposed to regulation and the data center hype cycle.

title: Contingency Spread Recovery for Public Benefit Pools
one_liner: Zero-upfront PBM pass-through audits sold to school and local-government benefit pools, paid as a share of verified savings, using a shadow pharmacy price list built from local independents' remits, with a slice of each fee paid back to those pharmacies.
lineage: mutation of I1266 ('Pharmacy-Side PBM Ledger for Employers'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Independent pharmacies squeezed by PBMs, refund floats and deserts

judges.fatal_flaw: Public-pool sales cycles are slow; PBM confidentiality clauses may block pharmacy data.
judges.note: Shadow price list turns a two-party join into a price-list problem; contingent, zero-PBM-money auditor with clean hands; niche capped near $30-100M.

judges.fatal_flaw: Pharmacy price pooling raises antitrust and confidentiality risk; long board sales cycles.
judges.note: Better than parent: public pools compel data, contingency, clean hands. But complex, needs 12+ pharmacies, and 10 customers in six months is unrealistic.

judges.fatal_flaw: Pharmacy contract confidentiality, antitrust exposure and PBM retaliation threaten the shadow price list.
judges.note: Clever shadow price list turns a two-party join into a price-list problem. Big prize, clean-hands contingency. Public-pool sales cycles are slow.

title: Tariff Surcharge Clawback for B2B Buyers
one_liner: A contingency-fee service that mines a buyer's 2025-26 supplier invoices for 'tariff surcharge' lines and recovers a share of the IEEPA refunds those suppliers are now collecting.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Recovering IEEPA tariff refunds and surcharges

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time windfall; buyers lack clear legal claim without explicit surcharge language.
judges.note: Sharp, timely non-consensus insight on refund transfers. Transient window, contested legal standing, and law firms or class actions are likelier winners.

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers lack legal claim to refunds without explicit pass-back language.
judges.note: Contingency pricing and timely windfall wave, but downstream legal right is weak and demand is a one-time spike, not a durable business.

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers lack legal claim without explicit pass-back terms; window closes within months.
judges.note: Anchored in the 2026 IEEPA refund windfall. Fastest cash of the batch, but a transient arbitrage that law firms and TariffRefund will crowd quickly.

title: Revenue-Integrity Diligence for Water System Acquirers
one_liner: The buyer of a small or mid-size water system pays for a 10-day, account-level scan of the target's billing, meters and parcels. It prices hidden revenue and revenue-quality risk before signing, then a success fee on prospectively recovered revenue funds the first-100-days fix.
lineage: mutation of I0388 ('Contingency Hunters for Unbilled Water Revenue'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Small water utilities: staffing, revenue leakage, lead lines and nitrate

judges.fatal_flaw: M&A diligence cycles are slow; data-room access gates first revenue.
judges.note: Moving the payer to the acquirer is smart: ownership change removes optics and back-billing risk. Original, but deal volume and sales cycle limit it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small acquirer pool and few deals make ten customers unlikely in six months.
judges.note: Buyer-paid, conflict-free diligence with clear pricing ROI; 10-day product fits deal windows. Slow to a volume of customers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few deals big enough to fund $50k diligence; long utility sales cycles.
judges.note: Moving the payer to the acquirer removes council optics and back-billing limits. Valuation-multiple logic is sound. Water M&A deal flow is thin but real.

title: AP-Inbox Implant Reconciler for Spine ASCs
one_liner: Forward your implant vendor invoices to one email address. We match each to the surgery, the payer's carve-out clause and the 835, and reopen the claim the day the invoice lands, so implant cost stops going unpaid.
lineage: mutation of I0708 ('Contingency Recovery of Unpaid Implant Carve-Outs'), type: sharpened
cluster: Provider revenue leaks and payer denials

judges.fatal_flaw: Ceiling limited to a few thousand surgeon-owned spine ASCs; incumbents may add feature.
judges.note: Invoice-arrives-after-claim event insight is sharp, contingency gets cash fast, zero integration; but narrow niche inside crowded revenue-cycle space.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Contingency-only, zero-integration, $5-30k leaks, dense ASC association channel, first dollars in weeks. Unit economics are excellent. Leak size is unproven until the audits.

judges.fatal_flaw: Specialist ASC billers already submit invoices routinely; Aspirion can bolt this on.
judges.note: Good insight: no system fires when an invoice arrives after the claim. AP inbox is a cheap integration surface. Still a crowded revenue-cycle space with a narrow wedge.

title: Pumper-Sampled Hydrogen and Helium Ground-Truth Registry
one_liner: Stop digging through what the industry failed to measure and start measuring it: pay lease pumpers to grab wellhead gas samples, assay them for hydrogen and helium, and build the depth-tagged registry that becomes the standard for what is under the ground.
lineage: mutation of I1085 ('Dry-Hole Atlas for Hydrogen, Helium, Geothermal'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Novel environmental and infrastructure data from satellites and crowd-sensing

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers are few speculative hydrogen juniors, many sampling in-house.
judges.note: Measures what industry never measured; bounty plus routine assay makes distribution cheap and campaigns sellable in months, but demand is thin and hype-dependent.

judges.fatal_flaw: Only ~100 explorers, many pre-revenue; free USGS data anchors price.
judges.note: Bounty-fed fresh sampling beats noisy archives; funded explorers need labels; unit margins fine. Niche buyer count and hype risk.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Inverts the archive-mining thesis: measure fresh gas with pumpers as sensors; operators already pay for assays. Odd, cheap, proprietary labels for a funded sector.

title: Grid-Readiness Model Audit for Data Center Lenders
one_liner: An independent checker for private-credit funds, banks and delay-in-start-up insurers that audits a borrower's large-load models and ride-through evidence and gives an energization-risk opinion, the same way financial-model auditors already serve project-finance lenders.
lineage: mutation of I0996 ('Grid-Code Models for AI Data Centers'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Getting power for large loads and storage

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs scarce EMT engineers and lender trust; niche worth roughly $15-25M.
judges.note: Applies the financial-model-auditor playbook to grid behavior for data center lenders. Strong why-now and independence angle, but expertise-gated and slow to first customer.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lenders may not demand this diligence item; needs EMT expertise and covenant adoption first.
judges.note: Independent-checker logic fits project finance and reachable via IE and law-firm channels. Demand is asserted, not proven. A $15-25M niche.

judges.fatal_flaw: Self-estimated $15-25M niche; lenders may not pay for grid-model opinions.
judges.note: Independent-checker culture applied to a black-box model; flips parent's threats into tailwinds. Thin analyst business, concentrated buyers, tied to AI debt cycle.

title: Cavity ID: Tool-of-Origin Evidence via Counsel
one_liner: Expert-grade 'which tool made this part, and when' reports, built from parts the brand already holds in the US and sold through China-facing IP law firms to brands whose ex-supplier is selling their product.
lineage: mutation of I0552 ('Supplier Divorce Protection: Tool Census and Overrun Forensics'), type: sharpened
cluster: US machine shops and reshoring manufacturers

judges.fatal_flaw: Only useful where the client owns enforceable IP; tiny forensic niche.
judges.note: Tool-wear-as-clock sold through counsel is clever and sharper than the parent. Still a boutique forensic service of roughly $1M ARR.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tool-wear dating is technically unproven; sold through few China-IP boutiques.
judges.note: Novel, urgent for affected brands, legal-budget buyer, cheap two-week blind validation. Evidence weight in Chinese enforcement uncertain; narrow market.

judges.fatal_flaw: Evidence useful only with enforceable IP; Chinese enforceability unproven.
judges.note: Tool wear as a clock, using parts already in US warehouses, is a truly non-obvious insight. Sold through counsel into legal budgets. Defensible via expert record.

title: Commissioning Passport: The Data Center Readiness Standard
one_liner: Invert the model: the sponsor pays a neutral party to verify hall readiness once, in a machine-readable ledger every lender, insurer, landlord and offtaker can read, which grows into the standard definition of ready-for-service and the trigger written into loan, lease and backstop documents.
lineage: mutation of I0365 ('Ground-Truth Diligence for GPU-Backed Lenders'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: Lenders may reject sponsor-paid attestation; people-bound service with incumbent IEs
judges.note: Issuer-pays verification as rating-agency analog in huge neocloud debt market; standard-setting upside. Rests on lenders accepting sponsor-paid attestation.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lenders may reject sponsor-paid attestation; payers are cash-strapped sub-IG sponsors.
judges.note: Verify-once readiness ledger as the RFS definition in loan documents is a bold standard play; bets on AI-capex continuing and lenders accepting sponsor-paid attestation.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs lenders to accept sponsor-paid attestation before any sponsor pays.
judges.note: Big prize if it becomes the standard, but few sponsors, chicken-and-egg lender acceptance, heavy commissioning expertise; unlikely ten payers in six months.

title: Independent Big-Meter Audits With Refund Guarantee
one_liner: A brand-neutral audit of a utility's 100-400 largest meters: AMI history is turned into a ranked, field-tested list of under-registering accounts. It is sold as a fixed-price small purchase, refunded if verified annual recovery is under 2x the fee.
lineage: mutation of I0388 ('Contingency Hunters for Unbilled Water Revenue'), type: sharpened
cluster: Small water utilities: staffing, revenue leakage, lead lines and nitrate

judges.fatal_flaw: Large-meter testing is established; recovery yields unproven; small-purchase limits vary by state.
judges.note: Refund guarantee neatly sidesteps contingency bans; AMI data fingerprint is a real new input. Feasible and boring-good, but insight is incremental and the ceiling modest.

judges.fatal_flaw: Municipal procurement is slow; 10 closes in six months is a stretch.
judges.note: Refund guarantee makes a $24k yes easy, economics are credible, and the independent test-label dataset is a moat. Brand-neutral angle escapes meter vendors.

judges.fatal_flaw: Consulting ceiling near $700K; vendors and rate consultants already test large meters.
judges.note: Refund guarantee neatly sidesteps contingency bans and sells fast under purchase limits. Small services business whose labeled test dataset is the only moat.

title: Deficiency-Suit Add-On Credit Audits for Consumer Defense Firms
one_liner: A flat-fee, 24-hour audit that rebuilds a repossession deficiency from the retail installment contract and shows the unearned add-on credits, notice defects and fee errors the lender or debt buyer left out, sold to the consumer-defense lawyers who already have the client and the deadline.
lineage: mutation of I0109 ('Payoff-Triggered Refund Recovery for Credit Unions'), type: sharpened
cluster: Unclaimed money: settlements, refunds, penalties and unpaid invoices

judges.fatal_flaw: Audit revenue is low single-digit millions; small defense firms and legal aid pay slowly.
judges.note: Much better buyer than the parent: lawyer with a deadline and fee-shifting. Audit-as-labeled-data for class counsel is the scale path but speculative.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low-budget buyers; $99 audits tiny; scale depends on unproven pattern-report sales.
judges.note: Right buyer finally (defense lawyers with standing, deadline, fee-shifting); defect patterns feed class-action data. $99 audits are tiny and unauthorized-practice risk remains.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small $99 ticket with human review per audit; defense firms are cash-strapped.
judges.note: Lawyers have the client, a 30-day deadline and fee-shifting; cheap audit easy to try; pattern reports to class counsel are real upside.

title: Ground-Truth Diligence for GPU-Backed Lenders
one_liner: Independent-engineer-style diligence and monthly monitoring on the part of a data center build that satellites cannot see: the last 90 days before ready-for-service.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: People-bound services bench with no software moat; incumbent engineers can copy.
judges.note: Hottest lender pain of the quarter with a quick $25K entry, but it is a consultancy that scales only via ratings.

judges.fatal_flaw: No site-access mechanism; looks like a slow IE competitor with weaker credentials.
judges.note: Same core insight as M1 but broad IE-style pitch with 40 milestones, monitoring and no access mechanism. Strictly dominated by its sharpened mutation.

judges.fatal_flaw: People-bound consulting with a thin moat; IEs can add the service.
judges.note: Interior commissioning truth is the scarce signal now that satellites cover the exterior. Lenders have budgets and a live neocloud-credit worry. Fast to first $25K sale.

title: Insurable-at-Closing: Pay-on-Closing Insurability Sheets for WUI Listings
one_liner: Listing agents order a 48-hour parcel evidence and carrier-routing sheet before a wildfire-zone home goes to market, and the seller pays a flat fee at closing only if the sale closes.
lineage: mutation of I1148 ('Parcel-Level Rebuttals to Wildfire Insurance Scores'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Homeowners and communities losing property insurance in high-risk areas

judges.fatal_flaw: Producer-compensation and RESPA limits; only about 6,000 annual sales in focus counties.
judges.note: Contingent on closing, a clean fee. Carrier-bind database is the real asset, but the market is tiny and needs a licensed partner.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs licensed placement partner; RESPA/producer-comp risk; year-one revenue about $0.2M.
judges.note: Escapes homeowner-appeal kits by owning the sale moment; pay-at-closing removes agent friction. Unverified fall-through data; partner agency already gives free quotes.

judges.fatal_flaw: RESPA and producer-compensation limits; $395 fee is thin; agents already route carriers.
judges.note: Treats insurability as a closing contingency and routes lots to carriers whose models read them correctly. Pay-on-close aligns well. Value depends on a licensed placement partner.

title: Federal-Agreement Lab for State SNAP QC Reviewers
one_liner: Sell calibration drills to the small, high-leverage group whose findings set the official error rate, the state QC reviewers, scoring them against a federal answer key and putting part of the fee at risk on the state-federal disagreement rate.
lineage: mutation of I1240 ('Flight simulator drills for county SNAP eligibility workers'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Benefit-rule changes: Medicaid work rules, SNAP and ACA cliffs

judges.fatal_flaw: Only 41 government buyers; ARR ceiling about $5-8M; slow procurement
judges.note: Strong dollar leverage per trained head and clever fee-at-risk. But 41 buyers cap ARR near $5-8M unless extended to other programs.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow state procurement; 20-25% of fee at risk on outcomes outside control.
judges.note: Huge dollar leverage per trained reviewer and an Alabama RFP proves purchasing, but only 41 buyers and government cycles.

judges.fatal_flaw: State procurement is slow; states may resist anything that raises error findings.
judges.note: H.R.1 turned QC findings into budget cliffs. The regression-to-federal-rate insight is non-obvious: calibrating a tiny reviewer group moves $100M. Fee at risk is credible.

title: Paid-But-Dark: Solar Loan Book Audit
one_liner: A fixed-fee audit and ongoing watch that tells credit unions, servicers and ABS holders which of their solar loans finance a roof that was never switched on. It then cures the worst ones through a supplier-neutral contractor bench.
lineage: mutation of I1175 ('Finish Crew: Stranded Solar Job Completion'), type: sharpened
cluster: Residential solar leftovers: orphaned systems, leases and liens

judges.fatal_flaw: Shrinking, event-driven distressed-solar niche; credit unions slow; GreenLancer may already cover.
judges.note: Lender blind spot (payments tracked, power not) is real and the audit sells under procurement thresholds. Market is a declining one-time wave.

judges.fatal_flaw: Event-driven, small book-audit revenue; GreenLancer's financiers may already cover holders.
judges.note: Missing-column insight (is the roof switched on) sold to the CRO's reserve problem; strong 2026 timing after Freedom Forever; fast to test on public data.

judges.fatal_flaw: Event-driven demand; GreenLancer may already serve servicers and credit unions.
judges.note: Selling to the CRO's reserve question, not loss-mitigation, is smart. Cheap automated audit, fixed fee under thresholds. Demand still unproven among credit unions.

title: Credit Bureau for Federal Drug-Refund Receivables
one_liner: Invert lend-and-learn into learn-and-license. A consortium data utility and certified servicer that makes Medicare price-negotiation refunds, later 340B rebates and Part B refunds, a standard scorable collateral class for any lender, wholesaler or credit fund.
lineage: mutation of I0499 ('Bridge Loans for Medicare Drug-Price Refunds'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Independent pharmacies squeezed by PBMs, refund floats and deserts

judges.fatal_flaw: Prize capped by small MFP float; CMS faster refunds or wholesaler control undercut it.
judges.note: Genuinely new asset class with no standard. A lender-neutral dilution data consortium has real compounding moat, and 340B and Part B expansion is plausible.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny lender universe, wholesalers control payment path, PHI burden; consortium needs scale first.
judges.note: Credit-bureau inversion is smart, but first customers need borrower data consent plus lender trust; Plenful could add a lender module.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cold-start consortium; CMS speeding refunds would shrink the float and lender demand.
judges.note: New statutory-refund asset class with no data owner. Credit-bureau inversion is original, float is large, standard files make a small-team build credible.

title: Recorder Rails: County-Funded Clean Index of Instruments
one_liner: AI re-indexing and compliance scans that counties buy from their own records-modernization funds. In return we hold the cleaned, entity-resolved index of every non-deed instrument, which becomes the data layer for assembly alerts and much else.
lineage: mutation of I0773 ('Courthouse Tape: Land-Assembly Radar for Infrastructure'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Land and property facts trapped in county records

judges.fatal_flaw: County sales grind; bulk commercial-use rules and incumbent county-software vendors.
judges.note: Smart inversion: counties pay to re-index, we keep the entity graph. Plausible by-product moat, but county-by-county grind and Tyler/Fidlar/Kofile can copy.

judges.fatal_flaw: County and vendor contracts may block bulk image access and resale of derived data.
judges.note: Inverts who pays: counties fund the re-index, we keep the cleaned national instrument graph. Real cornered-resource data asset with a live demand hook.

judges.fatal_flaw: County procurement cycles exceed six months; option-memo demand unverified.
judges.note: County-paid access is clever inversion, but government sales are slow, bulk-data rules vary by state, and downstream alert buyers are unproven.

title: UK Vet Price Panel for Investors and Insurers
one_liner: The first normalized, ownership-linked, time-series panel of UK vet prices, built from the price lists the CMA now forces every practice to publish, and licensed as a data feed to equity and credit investors, pet insurers and independent-practice bodies.
lineage: mutation of I1056 ('Unbundling Edits for Pet Insurance Claims'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Pet owners and insurers squeezed by rising vet bills

judges.fatal_flaw: Few funds cover UK vets; public prices are copyable; revenue ceiling roughly GBP 0.5M.
judges.note: Ownership join plus regulatory-mandated price lists create time-boxed, near-zero-cost data; investor budgets exist, but buyer pool is thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: History moat only months deep; niche UK data buyers; scrapable by anyone.
judges.note: Ownership-linked price panel is a neat regulation-created dataset with fast first buyers. Tiny prize, weak moat, and abandons the parent's insurer thesis.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few alt-data buyers for small-cap vet groups; ARR target looks inflated.
judges.note: Regulation created the data and the ownership join key. Unrecoverable time series gives a real window. Pivoting to investors escapes the balance-bill risk. Small but sharp.

title: Phantom-Load Registry: Land Records Meet Utility Queues
one_liner: A utility-funded vetting desk that joins courthouse land-assembly signals with co-op and municipal large-load inquiry logs, so it can say which 100-1,000 MW projects are real and which LLC families are shopping the same megawatts to five utilities.
lineage: hybrid of I0773 + I0079 (Courthouse Tape: Land-Assembly Radar for Infrastructure + Phantom Load Vetting Desk for Rural Utilities). Why stronger: The vetting desk alone is a services business with a thin data moat, and the tape alone fights for alt-data budgets with no ground-truth labels. Together, memo revenue funds data collection, utility outcomes label the data, and the pooled duplicate registry gets more valuable with each utility that joins. ACV rises, and utilities can be reached through co-op associations instead of cold outreach.
cluster: Land and property facts trapped in county records

judges.fatal_flaw: Collateral and study-fee rules make applicants self-prove, shrinking demand for outside vetting.
judges.note: Phantom data-center load is a defining 2026 problem; the join of land, permit and queue data plus outcome labels is hard to copy.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Burned co-ops, memo cost passes to applicants, association channel; memos fund data and outcomes label it. But collateral rules substitute for vetting.

judges.fatal_flaw: County-by-county recorder image access unproven; developers may not record options before announcing.
judges.note: Join of land, permit and queue data is clever, but bigger and more diffuse than the sharper intake-desk sibling; hybrid isn't clearly stronger.

title: Pay Home Inspectors to Find Lead Pipes
one_liner: A micro-bounty network that pays home inspectors, plumbers and water-heater installers to photograph where the service line enters the basement, with AI classification, so utilities can clear 'unknown material' lines for about $40 each instead of $500-3,000 each.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Small water utilities: staffing, revenue leakage, lead lines and nitrate

judges.fatal_flaw: States may require utility-overseen verification; inspector supply per utility is thin.
judges.note: Real LCRI deadline and funded utilities, cheap pilot POs. Two-sided supply density and regulatory acceptance are open; BlueConduit and VODA own the narrative.

judges.fatal_flaw: Third-party photos may not count; thin per-utility supply; inspector liability fears.
judges.note: Same pain as M1 but depends on opportunistic supply; M1 strictly improves on it.

judges.fatal_flaw: States may not accept third-party photos as verification; supply density per utility slow.
judges.note: Real insight: paid experts already stand beside the pipe. Compliance-forced, funded buyers; labor-arbitrage beats predictive modelers and mailers. Biggest prize in batch.

title: Referee Sampling for Black Mass and Battery Scrap
one_liner: Independent sampling and assay of black mass lots, using Pierre Gy's Theory of Sampling from mining, so scrap sellers and recyclers stop fighting over 5-15% payable swings.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Recycling quality, distressed capacity and battery/EPR compliance

judges.fatal_flaw: Inspection majors already offer sampling and umpire assay; capex-heavy station per site.
judges.note: Sharp mining-sampling insight, but SGS, Bureau Veritas and Intertek already sell independent sampling and umpire assay; distressed Western recyclers are weak buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Inspection majors may already offer it; parties may not bind to a referee.
judges.note: Gy sampling insight is real and disputes cost five figures per lot; free duplicate study sells itself. Needs capex and credibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: SGS, Bureau Veritas, Intertek already sell sampling and umpire assay; black mass handling is hazmat.
judges.note: Mining sampling theory imported into a chemist-run scrap trade is sharp and non-obvious; niche prize, and incumbents may claim they already do it.

title: Dual-Mode Genset Permits for Queued Campuses
one_liner: Design the air permit for new data center campuses before the generators are bought, so the backup fleet is legally curtailment-ready from day one and the fee is tied to energization date.
lineage: mutation of I0836 ('Air-Permit Unlock for Idle Data Center Diesel'), type: sharpened
cluster: Getting power for large loads and storage

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Smart kill-test via attorney memo, scrapeable permit leads, buyers with huge delay costs. Success fee depends on PJM accepting early energization, which is speculative.

judges.fatal_flaw: Fixed-fee consulting gated by a legal memo; low defensibility once playbook is known.
judges.note: Sharp timing and 50x buyer ROI on energization date, but a consulting business capped at a few million.

judges.fatal_flaw: Air-permit path may not close; consultants can copy; acceleration fee unattributable.
judges.note: Non-obvious: design the permit before buying engines. Energization date is the metric buyers care about. Legal flux and consultancies like Trinity limit defensibility.

title: Power Passport: Scoring Dead Factories on Amps, Permits
one_liner: A database and paid inspection report that rates shuttered Midwest plants on the things reshoring manufacturers actually need (utility service, slab, crane, transferable air and discharge permits) instead of square footage.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: US machine shops and reshoring manufacturers

judges.fatal_flaw: Unproven that brokers pay $1.5k-$3.5k; permit-transferability wedge is thin.
judges.note: Powered-shell thesis is right: amps and permits are the asset. But the buyer is wrong for a one-off report and the dataset is easy to copy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Brokers may refuse to pay $1.5k+; permit-transfer wedge is thin.
judges.note: Electrician-verified building record is a genuine gap and sellable one metro at a time. Willingness to pay is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Brokers may refuse to pay $1.5k+ per listing; permit transferability wedge is thin.
judges.note: Tangible physical-world insight: energized service, permits and cranes are the real asset, and data centers compete for the same shells. Verified-building data is unusual.

title: Well Covenant Trustee for Rural Data Center Counties
one_liner: A neutral program administrator writes, monitors and runs a county-mandated, developer-funded private-well protection covenant, where excess drawdown versus upgradient control wells triggers in-kind remediation with no lawsuit and no sensor sales.
lineage: mutation of I1172 ('Neutral Baselines and Neighbor Guarantees for Data Centers'), type: sharpened
cluster: Localities, utilities and landowners facing speculative data-center demand

judges.fatal_flaw: Drawdown attribution versus drought stays contested; narrower than the home-value guarantee.
judges.note: County attorney as real buyer solves the developer-admission problem; in-kind remedy and control-well triggers are credible but smaller in scope.

judges.fatal_flaw: County sales cycles and insurance-characterization risk delay revenue past six months.
judges.note: Clever county-mandated structure with developer as payer, but counsel opinion gates everything and government sales are slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow county adoption; neutral trustee takes liability exposure and needs credible hydrogeology.
judges.note: Sells the legal instrument, not sensors. County attorney as real buyer removes the developer's admission problem. Live permit politics make a template spreadable.

title: Failed-Part Bounty for Insurance Subrogation
one_liner: Pay plumbers a bounty to bag, photograph and chain-of-custody the pipe, supply line or fitting that failed, then sell the evidence and a brand-level failure database to insurers' subrogation units and manufacturers.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Singular / uncategorized

judges.fatal_flaw: Unproven that insurers pay $75-150 for claims they skip today.
judges.note: Clever price signal on destroyed evidence, easy shop recruitment, but buyer value unproven and per-part margin thin after courier and storage.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers may not pay for parts they would not pursue anyway.
judges.note: Memorable insight that plumbers destroy the evidence, but claim-less timing, courier logistics and manufacturer pushback on the failure database undercut it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Payer unclear: the plumber bags the part before any claim exists.
judges.note: Plumber is the true first notice of loss for the product; evidence is destroyed daily. Cheap bounty price signal plus a unique failure-rate dataset.

title: Courthouse Tape: Land-Assembly Radar for Infrastructure
one_liner: A daily feed that reads recorded option memoranda, leases and easements to show who is quietly assembling land for data centers, solar and transmission weeks before anyone announces it.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Land and property facts trapped in county records

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Image-level reading of recorded options plus an LLC graph is real alt-data alpha for developers and funds; county access is both moat and bottleneck.

judges.fatal_flaw: Bulk recorder access county by county; unclear developers record options pre-announcement.
judges.note: Developers already pay landmen for this; county-by-county access is the real work. Daily feed value depends on options being recorded before announcement, unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: County bulk-access unknown; moat is recorder access, not technology.
judges.note: Notary and return-to fingerprints plus mislabeled doc types are a clever, real insight tied to the land rush. Seller of intel to competing developers; access risk is county by county.

title: 48-Hour Verify List for Independent Floorplan Lenders
one_liner: A daily, capacity-capped list of the specific floored VINs an independent lender's auditor should physically verify in the next 48 hours, built from listing disappearance plus the lender's own payoff ledger, with a disposition classifier and per-dealer baselines that fix the noisy-signal problem.
lineage: mutation of I0218 ('Sold-Out-of-Trust Radar for Floorplan Lenders'), type: sharpened
cluster: Lenders and investors unable to verify collateral exists

judges.fatal_flaw: Listing-disappearance signal is noisy; Vero, SBS or NextGear can bolt it on.
judges.note: Sharpened to dispatch with per-dealer baselines and one-CSV integration; fastest to paid pilot, but small lender universe and bolt-on risk cap the prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Delist signal is noisy; small buyer universe; lenders slow to convert after free shadow run.
judges.note: Sharp fix to prior flaws; one-CSV data need, dispatch-capped output, audit-firm channel; precision unproven and Cox or Vero could bolt on.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small niche; a licensed listing feed makes the signal replicable by Vero or NextGear.
judges.note: Sharpened well: one-CSV ledger, per-dealer baselines, capacity-capped dispatch. Real 2025-26 fraud shock. Prize is only a few million dollars of ARR.

title: Supervised-Hours Bench for Counselors and Social Workers
one_liner: A managed group-supervision network and hour-logging platform that lets clinics fund the thousands of post-degree supervised hours gating counseling, MFT and social-work licenses.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Behavioral health and addiction care capacity

judges.fatal_flaw: State supervisor rules vary; supervisor liability and associate insurance credentialing unverified.
judges.note: Clear employer pain, cheap versus associate billings, strong unit economics, fast small-practice sales; incumbents sell to associates, not employers.

judges.fatal_flaw: State supervisor rules and payer credentialing vary; thin margins and weak why-now.
judges.note: Real, large bottleneck with an employer payer and fast first sales. Mostly a labor-arbitrage service with limited defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Many states restrict outside supervisors; payers often don't credential associates.
judges.note: Employer-paid supervision is a fair reframe, but the bottleneck is well known, the loan-cap why-now is weak, and logging software is commodity.

title: Delay-Risk Underwriting Desk for Data Center Insurers
one_liner: Sell Delay-in-Start-Up underwriters a 5-day hall-level readiness review and a portfolio 'collision calendar' so scarce DSU capacity can be written on more projects with fewer surprises, funded by the insured through a policy subjectivity, and later share in the premium.
lineage: mutation of I0365 ('Ground-Truth Diligence for GPU-Backed Lenders'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurance cycles are slow; carriers may not make outside review a subjectivity.
judges.note: Correlated-delay Collision Calendar is a genuine insight and the MGA end-state is a real company. First paid customer in six months is doubtful.

judges.fatal_flaw: Carriers rely on in-house risk engineers; insured-paid subjectivity unproven; year-long insurance cycles.
judges.note: Underwriters buy capacity, and the correlation calendar is smart. But insurance sales cycles are slow and carriers may not make outside reviews a subjectivity.

judges.fatal_flaw: Unproven that carriers will mandate outside review; insurance sales cycles slow.
judges.note: The correlated-pool insight (ten halls, one startup crew) is genuinely non-obvious. Buyer behavior is unvalidated and insurers may rely on in-house surveys.

title: Contingency Audit of Unbilled Plumbing Materials
one_liner: Reconcile a trade shop's supply-house invoices against its customer invoices and catch both parts that were bought but never billed and quiet supplier price drift, paid a percentage of what gets recovered.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Small trade and service firms underpricing and leaking margin

judges.fatal_flaw: ServiceTitan could bundle it; leakage rate is anecdotal and unverified.
judges.note: Huge reachable base of shops, free 48-hour audit, no-recovery-no-fee. Easiest first ten customers in the batch; thin moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: ServiceTitan AP or Kojo can bolt on matching; trades-shop ceiling is modest.
judges.note: Fastest path to cash via free audits and contingency fees; pooled price benchmark is a modest moat. Boring-trades-plus-LLM pattern, and a feature risk.

judges.fatal_flaw: Unbilled parts can't be re-billed retroactively; contingency attribution disputes; ServiceTitan AP overlaps.
judges.note: Freight-audit transplant to boring trades is the default contrarian move. Easy pilots via peer groups, but recovery is mostly prospective and the benchmark moat is speculative.

title: WhatsApp Voice-Note Superintendent for Spec Builders
one_liner: A bilingual coordinator-plus-AI service that runs daily crew confirmations, headcounts and re-sequencing for a builder's two dozen subs over WhatsApp voice notes, priced per house.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Small builders' crew coordination, permits and speed

judges.fatal_flaw: Labor-arbitrage service with no moat; any bilingual coordinator can copy.
judges.note: Interface-is-the-foreman's-WhatsApp insight is sound and first customers come in weeks. Vertical-AI-for-trades pattern with weak defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Crews may withhold headcounts amid ICE fear; value hinges on builder behavior change.
judges.note: Recurring $3-6K per builder, human-in-loop service reachable via builder associations, measurable saved crew-days; manual start proves value fast.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low-defensibility labor arbitrage; Procore and others can bolt on voice notes.
judges.note: ICE-driven crew volatility is a real shift and first customers are easy to land. It is a thin services business in the 'boring trades' pattern.

title: Dry-Hole Atlas for Hydrogen, Helium, Geothermal
one_liner: Re-read a century of scanned well logs and gas analyses, once treated as junk, to find natural hydrogen, helium and hot rock, and sell the resulting atlas to exploration companies by area of interest.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Novel environmental and infrastructure data from satellites and crowd-sensing

judges.fatal_flaw: USGS and SMU give structured layers free; only about 0.5% of wells show hydrogen.
judges.note: Original reframe of old data with real exploration interest, but small cash-poor juniors and thin lead counts limit revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Free USGS/SMU data covers the baseline; about 120 buyers cap subscription revenue.
judges.note: Real insight: old dud wells are new leads. Cheap to start and demo, but a small data-vendor market unless it later takes lease positions.

judges.fatal_flaw: Free USGS/SMU baselines cover structured data; buyers cash-poor, real leads rare.
judges.note: Elegant insight: data value flips when the commodity changes. Hydrogen, helium and geothermal rush is real. Moat is only the extraction pipeline.

title: Evac Cash: Payout When Ordered to Evacuate
one_liner: A few dollars a month buys a $500-$2,500 wire within hours of an official mandatory evacuation order for your address, covering hurricane, wildfire and burn-scar flood orders.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Fast parametric cash for weather and disaster shocks

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurance licensing plus adverse selection when buyers wait for the storm forecast.
judges.note: Legal-act trigger is elegant, but low-income buyers will not pre-pay, an MGA and fronting carrier come first, and funder-pays sales are slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Carrier could add an evacuation rider; funder-pays demand unproven.
judges.note: Legal-act trigger means near-zero basis risk and co-payers (employers, governments); El Niño timing sharp. Needs MGA and fronting carrier first.

judges.fatal_flaw: Correlated mass payouts, adverse selection and licensing; carriers could add a flat rider.
judges.note: Legal-act trigger removes basis risk; funder-pays model is original. Large population in evacuation zones, though distribution and underwriting are the real work.

title: Independent Answer Key for Synthetic Respondents
one_liner: Invert the referee: a neutral scoring authority that holds fresh, verified-human ground truth, and scores synthetic-respondent and digital-twin vendors against it in quarterly pre-registered, sealed-prediction benchmarks.
lineage: mutation of I0716 ('Independent Referee for Survey Panel Data'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Gatekeepers drowning in AI-generated submissions and bot responses

judges.fatal_flaw: Vendors may refuse scoring; two-sided cold start; $10-20k wave costs before revenue.
judges.note: Neutral sealed-prediction protocol is original, but eval benchmarks rarely monetize and insights buyers move slowly.

judges.fatal_flaw: Vendors can ignore it; vendor-paid scoring strains neutrality; fielding costs precede revenue.
judges.note: Neutral sealed-prediction scorer for synthetic respondents rides a hot category and wins either way. Standard-setter upside, fast founding-member pre-sales, explicit kill test.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs a costly human control panel and vendors willing to be scored.
judges.note: Sealed-prediction protocol is the right fix for training-data leakage. Wins whether synthetic respondents succeed or fail. Two-sided authority is hard to bootstrap quickly.

title: Carve-Out Audit Kit for Challenger ASC Billers
one_liner: A white-label implant carve-out engine for independent ASC billing companies, who use a free lookback on a prospect or new client as their sales weapon and split the recovered dollars with us.
lineage: mutation of I0708 ('Contingency Recovery of Unpaid Implant Carve-Outs'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Provider revenue leaks and payer denials

judges.fatal_flaw: Billers may already catch carve-outs; each payer contract needs reading.
judges.note: Biller channel solves trust and data access; free lookback is a real sales weapon; big per-facility dollars, but cash arrives slowly.

judges.fatal_flaw: Leakage may be under 2%; Aspirion could add carve-outs; commercial contracts only.
