judges.note: Biller-channel and switch-moment lookback is smart distribution, but leakage may be small at specialist billers and each payer contract needs hand reading.

judges.fatal_flaw: Implant leakage may be under 2%; billers resist tools that admit past misses.
judges.note: Challenger-biller channel neatly solves trust and data access, but leakage is unproven, commercial-only, and RCM is crowded.

title: The True Acceptance Map for Rural Transfers
one_liner: Voice AI agents call every receiving psychiatric unit and specialty hospital each night to learn what they will actually accept, and rural ERs text a number to find out who will say yes.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Rural and underserved patients who cannot reach care

judges.fatal_flaw: Rural ERs have little budget; facilities may refuse bot calls; registries can copy
judges.note: Tacit acceptance rules are real, unmapped data; founder binder gives instant start. Small paying base of rural ERs and state-fund dependence cap the prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Intake staff may refuse or distrust robot calls; rules change with each shift.
judges.note: Tacit acceptance rules and the human decider are the real data, which registries miss. RHTP money helps, but voice-agent core is a known pattern.

judges.fatal_flaw: Facilities may not disclose rules to bots; rural ERs and states pay slowly.
judges.note: Acute pain and RHTP funding tailwind, truly novel data. Weak ER willingness to pay; state sales slow; start human-curated, not voice AI.

title: Dispatch-Eligibility Registry for Backup Generators
one_liner: Become the neutral system of record for whether each backup generator may legally run for the grid right now, starting as a Texas SB 6 compliance product and growing into the rail that ERCOT, PJM, utilities and aggregators check before dispatch.
lineage: mutation of I0836 ('Air-Permit Unlock for Idle Data Center Diesel'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Getting power for large loads and storage

judges.fatal_flaw: Federal rules bar emergency engines from capacity dispatch; regulator acceptance unproven
judges.note: Regulation-forced demand and rail potential are strong, but real value hinges on regulators accepting the ledger and engines' emergency-use limits.

judges.fatal_flaw: Emergency-engine rules bar grid dispatch regardless of registry; regulator acceptance unproven.
judges.note: Run-hour ledger as scarce commodity is clever and SB 6 forces demand. Rides the crowded data-center-power theme and may be DIY-able; dispatch rail is speculative.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs regulators to accept a private ledger; emergency-engine rules limit dispatch anyway.
judges.note: Registry/rail ambition with network-effect hand-waving. SB 6 compliance entry is real but small. Heroic reliance on regulator and aggregator adoption.

title: Tooling Title Diligence for Small-Brand Acquirers
one_liner: A fixed-fee, 5-day report that tells buyers of $2M-$50M product companies which molds the target legally owns, where they physically sit, and whether the factory is already selling the target's product.
lineage: mutation of I0552 ('Supplier Divorce Protection: Tool Census and Overrun Forensics'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: US machine shops and reshoring manufacturers

judges.fatal_flaw: Small market; M&A lawyers and QoE firms can add tooling checks.
judges.note: Selling to the buyer at peak willingness to pay is a real improvement over the parent. Sellable quickly via brokers, but a diligence report is a thin standalone business.

judges.fatal_flaw: Weak defensibility; QoE firms or M&A lawyers can bundle it, and deal volume is small.
judges.note: Sells to the buyer at peak willingness to pay; findings convert directly to closing conditions or price cuts. Fast to launch, modest ceiling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Chinese factories won't confirm tool title quickly; deal volume with tooling risk is modest.
judges.note: Real blind spot in small-brand deals; $4.9K is rounding error at wire time; broker channel is accessible. Needs supplier cooperation inside five days.

title: Load-Proven Warranty Wrap for Data Halls
one_liner: Invert the parent: instead of chasing OEMs for owners as warranties expire, run a standardized load-proof test before expiry, fix what the OEM owes for free, then sell a capacity-backed warranty wrap that covers the post-expiry tail, priced from a proprietary fleet failure database.
lineage: mutation of I0229 ('Warranty Clock Recovery Audits for Idle Halls'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Warranty claims left unfiled

judges.fatal_flaw: Unproven reinsurer appetite; equipment-breakdown insurers may already cover this tail
judges.note: Test-then-underwrite loop is smart, but the insurance wrap needs capacity providers and OEM clocks mostly start at startup, narrowing exposure.

judges.fatal_flaw: Commissioning firms already load-test; insurer capacity and MGA licensing make the wrap slow.
judges.note: Beats its parent: neutral cross-vendor failure data could price post-warranty risk for lenders, but the test phase is commissioning and the moat accrues slowly.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurance wrap needs reinsurer, MGA licensing and failure data years away.
judges.note: Phase 1 load testing is a commodity commissioning service. The big money needs capital and regulated risk-taking. Parent's collection flaw merely moved.

title: Continuity Retainer for One-Licensee Funeral Homes
one_liner: Key-person insurance for funeral homes: a bench of pre-credentialed licensed directors and embalmers who step in within 24-48 hours when the owner is sick, burned out or gone, with a built-in path to succession.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Independent funeral homes facing key-person, overnight and consolidation pressure

judges.fatal_flaw: Manager-in-charge rules may bar temporary designation; liability and bench density.
judges.note: Single license-holder as single point of failure is a sharp insight, and the succession pipeline into funeral-home buys is the real prize. Legal and supply risks are heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: State boards may not allow temporary manager-in-charge, voiding the 24-48 hour activation promise.
judges.note: Locum-style model with real owner exposure and scrappy launch. But insurance-like retainer for a rare event, state-law uncertainty, thin density, slow trust-building.

judges.fatal_flaw: State manager-in-charge rules may block 24-48 hour interim coverage; adverse selection, liability.
judges.note: Genuinely out-of-the-box: owner's license is a single point of failure, and succession pipeline is clever, but small prize and unverified legality.

title: The Reference Panel: Neutral Ruler for E/M Levels
one_liner: A neutral, triple-blind coder-and-physician panel that measures how reliable any E/M level really is, and sells that measurement to scribe vendors, payers and providers who are now fighting over it.
lineage: mutation of I0389 ('Independent Auditor for AI-Scribed Billing'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Proving AI controls and human review to insurers, auditors and clients

judges.fatal_flaw: Human-panel margins scale poorly; audit incumbents can rebrand the same service within quarters.
judges.note: Selling the disagreement rate as a noise floor is clever and timely amid payer downcoding, but regulator credibility takes years.

judges.fatal_flaw: Neutrality across payers and providers is hard; VMG, MDaudit can copy; slow compliance sales.
judges.note: Disagreement-rate insight is sharp and compliance budgets exist during disputes; three-sided neutrality and credibility take years.

judges.fatal_flaw: Neutrality unproven across three sides; labor-heavy; incumbent auditors could rebrand within quarters.
judges.note: Selling the measured disagreement rate is clever; every incumbent becomes a customer, and contested-encounter files can pay early. Credibility is slow to build.

title: Settlement Passports for Florida High-Rise Condos
one_liner: A satellite-radar settlement history for every Florida condo tower, sold as the cheap first page of the milestone-inspection and reserve-study file.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Novel environmental and infrastructure data from satellites and crowd-sensing

judges.fatal_flaw: Nothing mandates buying it; no technology moat; boards may avoid documenting settlement risk.
judges.note: Cheap free-data processing, engineer-resale channel, fast first sales; pitch as stability proof; Estructura and TRE Altamira can copy.

judges.fatal_flaw: No technology moat; incumbents or open-source stacks replicate; small price per building.
judges.note: Real deadline and board pain, wholesale via engineers, stability-as-underwriting-asset is smart; ceiling is modest unless it expands beyond Florida.

judges.fatal_flaw: Boards avoid data that creates disclosure liability; no technology moat.
judges.note: Free radar data and Surfside rules give a real hook. But TRE Altamira and open-source tools make it copyable, and engineers may see it as liability.

title: Rural Vet Call Logs as Outbreak Early Warning
one_liner: Producers call the vet before they call the state. Anonymized weekly counts of abortions, maggot wounds, sudden deaths and respiratory clusters are a leading indicator that traders, insurers and packers will pay for.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Farm and ranch risks: disease, cash, storage and machinery

judges.fatal_flaw: Vet reporting duties, MNPI exposure and thin vet incentive undermine data supply.
judges.note: Clever alt-data insight: the vet's phone is the earliest sensor. Screwworm timing is perfect, but the revenue story is thin without the herd-count hook.

judges.fatal_flaw: Free government data and legal exposure cap price; vets gain little.
judges.note: Real signal in the screwworm era, but vets must report suspects, supply is unpaid volunteers, and selling to funds invites MNPI risk.

judges.fatal_flaw: Vets lack incentive to report weekly; data quality is noisy and the buyer pool is thin.
judges.note: Vets as the earliest sensor is a good insight, and screwworm in 2026 gives it urgency. Alt-data buyers exist, but signal quality is unproven.

title: Ride-Through Witness: Measure-First Large-Load Network
one_liner: Invert the parent's model-before-energization: ingest the UPS logs and power-quality waveforms sites already record, join them with grid-side PMU data, and auto-produce ISO-format ride-through and oscillation reports, growing into the reference data network that ISOs, OEMs and insurers rely on.
lineage: mutation of I0996 ('Grid-Code Models for AI Data Centers'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Getting power for large loads and storage

judges.fatal_flaw: Operators have little incentive to hand over logs proving their own load trips.
judges.note: Compliance-driven wedge with a network-effect story, but sales to cautious operators need rare engineers and logs they would rather not share. 'AI needs power' pattern.

judges.fatal_flaw: Operators reluctant to share facility data; OEM and PQ-meter vendors can add analytics.
judges.note: Better than parent: software-first, ingests data sites already log, neutral cross-vendor network is a real cornered resource. Still a hot, crowded theme.

judges.fatal_flaw: Operators may refuse to hand forensic logs to a third party reporting to ISOs.
judges.note: Joining facility-side recorders with grid PMUs is smart and timed to NOGRR282. Data-network and standard upside; concierge audits give a fast start.

title: Coder-Signed Reasonable-Value Reports for Injury Defense
one_liner: A 48-hour, coder-certified benchmark report that tells defense lawyers and auto carriers what a letter-of-protection medical bill is actually worth.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Small litigation practices lacking evidence, records and benchmark tools

judges.fatal_flaw: Coder is not an expert witness; benchmark itself is copyable from free CMS data.
judges.note: Defense firms already pay $3-5k for experts; $349 report with 100-firm cold outreach is a fast close. Moat is only the coder bench.

judges.fatal_flaw: Florida statute and free CMS data let carriers copy the benchmark cheaply; Enlyte nearby.
judges.note: Coder bench with cross-examination-proof methodology is a real gap, but low price points, commodity inputs and mismatched why-now make it copyable.

judges.fatal_flaw: Florida statute and free CMS data commoditize the benchmark; coder bench is services.
judges.note: Fastest path to revenue and strong tort-reform timing. Services-heavy with modest ceiling; moat is a credentialed bench that survives cross-examination.

title: Retailer-Mandated Vulnerability Desk, Paid by Suppliers
one_liner: EU retailers and distributors put the desk on their approved-provider list for connected private-label and marketplace products, and their non-EU suppliers pay per SKU family, the way suppliers already pay retailer-nominated test labs, while the retailer gets a live exposure dashboard for its whole connected catalogue.
lineage: mutation of I0374 ('Outsourced 24-Hour Vulnerability Reporting Desk (CRA)'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: EU digital product laws for small connected-device makers

judges.fatal_flaw: Retailer mandate unproven; tooling layer crowded; small-firm 24h fine exemption.
judges.note: Nominated-lab buyer chain is a real insight fixing the parent's distribution, yet it remains a thin compliance service with commoditised tooling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Long EU retail procurement; needs 24/7 desk, named EU analysts, indemnity cover.
judges.note: Retailer mandate multiplies payers per sale and CRA deadlines are real, but enterprise sales cycles and staffing burden are heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Retailers rarely mandate a single vendor; long enterprise sales cycles.
judges.note: Changing the buyer chain (retailer mandates, supplier pays) fixes the parent's insurance-sale problem. Mandate leverage is plausible but slow to land.

title: Walkaway: PBM Offer Modeler Sold Through Associations
one_liner: A local-first tool that turns an independent pharmacy's own remits and invoices into a keep-or-drop answer for each January 1 PBM network offer, sold as a member benefit through state pharmacy associations.
lineage: mutation of I1266 ('Pharmacy-Side PBM Ledger for Employers'), type: sharpened
cluster: Independent pharmacies squeezed by PBMs, refund floats and deserts

judges.fatal_flaw: Roughly $13M ceiling; PSAOs may already offer contract modeling to members.
judges.note: Hard Q4 decision deadline and local-first design is smart, but by its own math the ceiling is about $13M and the customer base is shrinking.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Hard January decision date, $299 versus accountant hours, association channel, local-first dodges antitrust and cold start. Unverified risk: PSAOs may already model offers.

judges.fatal_flaw: PSAOs may already offer contract modeling; small ceiling around $13M.
judges.note: Priced-exit framing plus local-first architecture fixes the parent's cold start and antitrust issues; live Q4 deadline. Ceiling is small and PSAOs may already offer it.

title: Big-Meter Replacement Fund, Repaid by Verified Uplift
one_liner: A meter-brand-neutral fund buys, installs and owns a utility's worst large meters at zero upfront cost. The utility repays 70% of measured incremental revenue for up to 5 years, with an open verification protocol that makes it an underwritable asset class.
lineage: mutation of I0388 ('Contingency Hunters for Unbilled Water Revenue'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Small water utilities: staffing, revenue leakage, lead lines and nitrate

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs $250-400k capital and municipal procurement before the first dollar of repayment.
judges.note: Attractive 1-2 year payback and clever verification standard, but it is a financing business needing council approval, capital and non-appropriation workarounds.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs capital up front; non-appropriation and procurement rules slow municipal contingent contracts.
judges.note: Reframes meter replacement as financing, repaid by verified uplift with open M&V protocol; real asset-class potential, but needs fund capital and slow municipal contract approval.

judges.fatal_flaw: Municipal contingent-payment and appropriation law; yield unproven; ESCOs already do shared-savings metering.
judges.note: Verified-uplift asset class is a big idea if M&V works. Needs capital and utility procurement patience, and the competitor escape is thinner than claimed.

title: Air-Permit Unlock for Idle Data Center Diesel
one_liner: Turn the ~55 GW of idle data center backup generators into dispatchable capacity by solving the air-permit problem instead of the hardware problem.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Getting power for large loads and storage

judges.fatal_flaw: Federal emergency-engine rules likely force costly Tier 4 retrofits before any capacity sales.
judges.note: Largest prize in the batch (55 GW of idle capacity), sharp why-now, genuinely non-consensus. Legal feasibility is the open question; a permit playbook is the moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: Federal emergency-engine rules bar capacity revenue without costly reclassification and Tier 4 retrofits.
judges.note: Biggest prize in batch: capacity already built, blocked by permits. Genuine seam, but the data-center power theme is crowded and operators resist running gensets.

judges.fatal_flaw: Emergency-engine rules bar income use; reclassification needs Tier 4 retrofits and re-permitting.
judges.note: Engines can't legally be counted as capacity without costly reclassification. Retrofit financing is capital-heavy. The mutations fix this better.

title: Solos Refer, We File: National Delay-Suit Bench
one_liner: Invert the tool model: a lawyer-owned litigation bench that takes stuck cases referred by immigration solos, files at industrial speed for about 60% of the boutique price, and pays the referring lawyer a fee share, building a national referral network and the full-cycle dataset as a by-product.
lineage: mutation of I1062 ('Delay-Suit Rails for Stuck Immigration Cases'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Immigrant households and workers: status deadlines and paperwork

judges.fatal_flaw: Fee-division and MSO ethics rules vary by state; filing volume is small
judges.note: Referral channel into a lawyer-owned bench is clever and fast to first cases. Fee-splitting ethics rules, hostile districts, small filing volume cap scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Fee-split ethics rules and need for a litigator cofounder gate launch state by state.
judges.note: Desperate paying clients, free referral channel via solos, about $1,450 contribution per case, 10 cases fileable in 30 days. Market volume is the cap.

judges.fatal_flaw: Fee-split ethics rules, fast mootness and a thin data moat.
judges.note: Referral-bench insight about solos not wanting to be counsel of record is plausible. Legal-AI services territory, ethics-gated, and a boutique already owns the niche.

title: Contingency Hunters for Unbilled Water Revenue
one_liner: Find the 'ghost parcels' and slow big meters that leak revenue out of a utility, using assessor rolls, building footprints, imagery and billing data, and get paid 20-30% of what is recovered so the city risks nothing.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Small water utilities: staffing, revenue leakage, lead lines and nitrate

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow municipal procurement; some states restrict contingency contracts; ghost-parcel half is weak.
judges.note: Clear contingency pitch and free-scan sales motion; large-meter under-registration is real. Solid services business, not a venture outcome.

judges.fatal_flaw: Municipal procurement slow; contingency contracts restricted; ghost-parcel half is weak.
judges.note: Real large-meter under-registration money and zero-risk pitch, but meter-test firms and rate consultants already sell similar; maybe 1-2 customers in six months.

judges.fatal_flaw: Meter vendors already sell this; ghost parcels rare; contingency contracting restricted.
judges.note: Large-meter under-registration is well known in the water industry. Contingency recovery is workable but unoriginal, with a weak why-now.

title: Contingency Recovery of Unpaid Implant Carve-Outs
one_liner: Find and collect the implant and device carve-out payments that hospitals and surgery centers are owed but never bill, because the invoice lives in accounts payable and not in the billing office.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Provider revenue leaks and payer denials

judges.fatal_flaw: ASC billers may already submit invoices; commercial-only; incumbents can add it.
judges.note: Fastest path to cash: free lookback, contingency, clear dollars found. Insight real but sits in crowded RCM and underpayment recovery, so defensibility is weak.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Contingency, zero-risk free lookback, $5-50k per case, reachable surgeon-owners, first collections within weeks. Specialist billers may already catch some, but weak-billing ASCs leak.

judges.fatal_flaw: Generic revenue-cycle recovery; ASC billers already handle carve-outs; Aspirion can copy.
judges.note: Plain contingency recovery in a crowded revenue-cycle space. Superseded by I0708-M1, which has the sharper AP-trigger insight.

title: Agency E&O Insurers Fund AI-Exclusion File Reviews
one_liner: The insurers and endorsed programs that cover insurance agencies pay to put an AI-exclusion review and a client-acknowledgment file behind every commercial renewal their insured agencies handle. It is funded as loss control, in the way cyber insurers fund security scans, and the agency pays little or nothing.
lineage: mutation of I1133 ('Renewal Radar for Silent AI Exclusions'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Proving AI controls and human review to insurers, auditors and clients

judges.fatal_flaw: Carrier sales cycles run 3-6 months; value tied to one transient exclusion wave.
judges.note: Insurer-funded loss control is a better payer than agencies, and the E&O application hook is clever. Slow to close and narrow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Agencies must do voluntary work; carrier cycles run 3-6 months before first real revenue.
judges.note: Timely 1/1/2027 deadline; E&O carrier pays regardless of duty-to-advise, so loss-control funding is smart. Association-endorsed concierge pilot gets first cash.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers; carriers may not fund loss control before any AI-exclusion claims exist.
judges.note: Payer inversion to E&O carriers who pay regardless of duty is clever, but speculative demand, slow carrier procurement, and a free-tracker-crowded exclusion niche.

title: Same-Week MFP Refunds for Senior-Care Pharmacies
one_liner: A refund-purchase facility for independent long-term-care pharmacies that becomes the payee of record on Medicare's negotiated-price refunds and pays out within two business days, underwritten claim by claim.
lineage: mutation of I0499 ('Bridge Loans for Medicare Drug-Price Refunds'), type: sharpened
cluster: Independent pharmacies squeezed by PBMs, refund floats and deserts

judges.fatal_flaw: CMS or wholesalers could shorten refund timing, deleting the float within quarters.
judges.note: Policy-lag bridge financing on a statutory refund stream, sharpened to large-float LTC pharmacies. Real money, but capital-heavy, window short, wholesalers hold the payment path.

judges.fatal_flaw: Wholesaler weekly debit controls the refund path; CMS may speed payments; small market.
judges.note: Real, measurable float and good LTC focus, but payee-of-record is unproven. Capital-hungry specialty finance with a policy-fix window risk.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs lending capital; wholesalers control payment path; credit risk on cash-poor pharmacies.
judges.note: Public, measured pain and a fresh policy window. Balance-sheet business with unproven payee control and regulatory disclosure overhead; not scrappy.

title: AltSchool Without Buildings: Disability Programs in Host Schools
one_liner: AltSchool burned $170M+ building its own schools; in Texas, the new voucher money can only reach accredited schools with two years of history, so rent that eligibility by running clinician-led disability programs inside half-empty accredited private schools.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Microschools, homeschoolers and shrinking districts

judges.fatal_flaw: Accreditor or Comptroller may treat hosted programs as rented accreditation; thin margins.
judges.note: Three-way arbitrage on Texas voucher rules is real and urgent. Existential legal ambiguity, special-ed liability, and unit economics that may not cover clinicians.

judges.fatal_flaw: Accreditor or TEA may treat hosted programs as renting accreditation, killing the model.
judges.note: Biggest TAM here, repeatable across ESA states, strong why-now. Rule-arbitrage is fragile and special-ed operating liability is real.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hosted-program legality and accreditor acceptance unresolved; 10 students barely fund a clinician.
judges.note: Strong TEFA tailwind and urgent parents, but depends on renting accreditation, which regulators may reject. Payroll-heavy thin margins.

title: Subpoena-Ready Rate Cards for Lien-Based Clinics
one_liner: Invert the parent by selling the coder bench to the clinics being attacked, using their own ledgers to defend their prices and build the industry's only record of what LOP care actually collects.
lineage: mutation of I0428 ('Coder-Signed Reasonable-Value Reports for Injury Defense'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Small litigation practices lacking evidence, records and benchmark tools

judges.fatal_flaw: Clinic-paid rate memos carry little weight in court; fee-splitting and anti-kickback exposure.
judges.note: Fear purchase with budget and a data-index upside, but selling to the attacked clinics creates an issuer-pays credibility problem and regulatory exposure.

judges.fatal_flaw: Issuer-pays premium memos may be discounted by courts; healthcare fee-sharing and kickback exposure.
judges.note: Subpoena is a fear purchase with budget; clinic ledgers are a rare data asset. Credibility conflict and cash-tight clinics cap early adoption.

judges.fatal_flaw: Issuer-pays conflict undermines credibility; regulatory risk if rate cards read as justifying inflated bills.
judges.note: Smart inversion: subpoena as fear purchase, clinic ledgers as proprietary realized-value data. Credibility and ethics are shaky; Florida statute shrinks the benchmark gap.

title: Section-Level Hydrogen and Helium Leads for Landmen
one_liner: Sell 90-day exclusive, page-linked lists of Nemaha-corridor sections with hydrogen or helium evidence buried in old mud logs, DST reports and driller notes, to the landmen and lease shops who spend the first dollars of every junior's program.
lineage: mutation of I1085 ('Dry-Hole Atlas for Hydrogen, Helium, Geothermal'), type: sharpened
cluster: Novel environmental and infrastructure data from satellites and crowd-sensing

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny cash-poor buyer pool; leads leak once one lease shop acts.
judges.note: Time-boxed lead exclusivity is a smart pricing frame for hype-driven hydrogen leasing, but buyer pool is tiny, cash-poor and exclusivity is unenforceable.

judges.fatal_flaw: Landmen execute geologists' targets; they rarely pay for geoscience leads.
judges.note: Original and cheap to start with VLM extraction. The market is small, hype-driven and unproven. Underlying data is public, so defensibility is weak.

judges.fatal_flaw: Landmen follow client targets; tiny buyer pool; VLM extraction easily replicated.
judges.note: Time-boxed exclusive leads on a live hydrogen lease rush, with a 'do not lease' list. Sharp wedge but thin moat and a small market.

title: Keep-Warm: Preserving Power in Idle Plants
one_liner: Invert the database: instead of scoring dead plants once, sell a monthly service that keeps their electrical service alive and monitored, then turn 200 preserved shells into a right-of-first-offer inventory and, later, a balance-sheet powered-shell bank.
lineage: mutation of I0820 ('Power Passport: Scoring Dead Factories on Amps, Permits'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: US machine shops and reshoring manufacturers

judges.fatal_flaw: Premium-credit assumption unverified; REO owners buy preservation on lowest bid.
judges.note: Recurring monitoring is a better model than a one-off report and avoids the data competitors. But demand is a tiny owner pool and pivots into hardware ops.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurer premium credit and buyer premium for energized shells are unproven.
judges.note: Recurring field service for REO plants is concrete and original, but demand for preserved amps is speculative; servicer sales slow; fund stage needs capital.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurer premium credit and owner willingness to pay are unproven.
judges.note: Right non-obvious claim: idle plants' energized service is the asset, now valuable for AI power scarcity. Recurring service plus right-of-first-offer inventory. Operationally heavy.

title: Dead Capital: Succession Kits for Diaspora Families
one_liner: A flat-fee, advocate-supervised 'estate file' service that gets a dead parent's or grandfather's land, shares and dormant accounts legally transferred, sold to the adult children who pay from Nairobi, Dallas or Dubai.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Diaspora families managing death, care and property across borders

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Frozen-land succession is a huge, non-consensus market; diaspora payer, flat fee, WhatsApp-first start, field-agent moat; legal-practice boundaries manageable.

judges.fatal_flaw: About $150 flat fee cannot fund field agents across 1-3 year succession cases.
judges.note: Real diaspora pain and a novel coordination angle. Thin per-file economics, requires on-ground Kenyan operations, advocate-supervision limits, slow cash cycle.

judges.fatal_flaw: Advocates and informal agents already serve it; weak why-now; thin per-file margins.
judges.note: Sibling-coordination insight is decent, but it is a post-death, advocate-adjacent service. M3 supersedes it with a more distinctive angle.

title: Mixed-Lot Calf Referee With Brix Price Formulas
one_liner: An independent, photo-stamped Brix grade taken at the broker's loading dock that turns a blind mixed-dairy calf lot into a formula-priced lot, so the best dairies stop subsidizing the worst and disputes get settled by schedule, not argument.
lineage: mutation of I0617 ('Immune-Graded Beef-on-Dairy Calves With Warranty'), type: sharpened
cluster: Farm and ranch risks: disease, cash, storage and machinery

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny market: about $1.2M at 15 brokers; buyers can self-test for $1.
judges.note: Clever formula-pricing mechanism that fixes the lemons discount, but a niche calf-brokering sliver with little room to grow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low ceiling (about $1.2M) and sellers may keep trusting source-dairy reputation.
judges.note: Cheapest test in batch: two techs, $300 gear, success-based fee, hard kill gates. Real lemons-discount pain; scrappy and fast, but small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny ceiling (about $1M) and weak moat; self-testing could substitute.
judges.note: Sharper than the parent: the lemons discount and pre-agreed price formula drive the sale, not the measurement. Day-45 gates are honest. Ag niche, but a real insight.

title: Widow-First Retention Drills for Wealth Advisors
one_liner: Sell independent advisors an annual 'if one of us dies' rehearsal for couples, because the defection risk sits at the first spouse's death, not with the kids.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Hospice, dying and the first weeks of bereavement

judges.fatal_flaw: Vault vendors or consultants can copy the ritual; weak defensibility.
judges.note: Widow-retention is a real, under-targeted insight and RIAs buy quickly. But it is a service ritual plus thin software, closer to a feature than a platform.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Reachable buyers, clear ROI per retained widow, hand-run pilots at $2.5k. Fast to first dollars but thin product, easily copied by advisor-consultants.

judges.fatal_flaw: Ritual is copyable by consultants; software layer is commoditized.
judges.note: Widow-defection is a known wealth-management talking point, not a hidden insight. Drill concept is fresh, but defensibility is low and advisors may balk.

title: Megawatt Credit Bureau with Bonded Collateral
one_liner: Invert the vetting desk: real developers pay to be rated, utilities accept the rating for lower deposits, and the company eventually underwrites large-load security bonds off the physical-readiness data, so regulators' collateral rules become the market instead of the threat.
lineage: mutation of I0079 ('Phantom Load Vetting Desk for Rural Utilities'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Localities, utilities and landowners facing speculative data-center demand

judges.fatal_flaw: Revenue needs utility acceptance and surety capacity first; issuer-paid rating conflict.
judges.note: Collateral rules create a substitute market needing a readiness underwriter. Sharp insight, big upside if bonds work, but multi-party chicken-and-egg within six months.

judges.fatal_flaw: Worthless unless utilities accept the rating; bond phase needs surety capacity.
judges.note: Issuer-paid rating without regulatory or utility acceptance is a credential nobody honors. Surety underwriting is a heavy capital and licensing leap.

judges.fatal_flaw: Whole thesis hinges on utilities accepting an issuer-paid rating for deposit relief.
judges.note: Turns collateral rules into a market; bond economics are big and why-now is sharp. Chicken-and-egg acceptance risk, but the kill test is explicit.

title: Canary Humans: Leak-Testing ID Verification Vendors
one_liner: Put consenting, instrumented real people through a platform's ID and age checks, then prove whether the vendor kept, leaked or resold their documents.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Buyers unable to verify vendor, algorithm or AI-safety claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Leaks are rare; null attestations are weak evidence; vendors may object
judges.note: Honeytoken audit of ID vendors is original and timely after breaches, but null results sell poorly and real ID numbers cannot be canaries.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low leak base rate; attestations mostly say nothing found.
judges.note: Novel honeytoken approach to a real trust gap, but ID numbers cannot be canaries and vendors may treat enrolment as ToS violation.

judges.fatal_flaw: Leaks are rare, so attestations mostly say 'nothing found'; vendors may object to enrolments.
judges.note: Honeytokens applied to ID verifiers is original and timed to IDScan and EU age-check wave. Buyers want protection, not proof; evidence is probabilistic.

title: Dairy-Backed Calf Guarantee Pool With Immune Screening
one_liner: Invert the parent: instead of selling buyers a verification and later insuring the raiser, make the dairy, who controls colostrum, warrant its own graded calves for 21 days, with our grade as the price of admission and a reserve pool we administer, growing into a mutual or captive with an MGA and reinsurer behind it.
lineage: mutation of I0617 ('Immune-Graded Beef-on-Dairy Calves With Warranty'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Farm and ranch risks: disease, cash, storage and machinery

judges.fatal_flaw: Pooled warranty may be unlicensed insurance; stated ceiling only $10-30M revenue.
judges.note: Spence-style guarantee flips moral hazard cleverly and beef-on-dairy is booming. Capital-light mutual path is plausible, but the prize is small and licensing is messy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Reserve pool paying claims is unlicensed insurance; early fees tiny per dairy.
judges.note: Warranty by the party controlling the risk flips moral hazard; beef-on-dairy boom makes calves valuable. Original, but slow-building and structurally regulated.

judges.fatal_flaw: Pooled dairy warranty likely counts as insurance; needs reserves and licensed MGA.
judges.note: Clever inversion fixing moral hazard, but about $20k per dairy per year and regulatory and capital burden before real scale.

title: Orphan Lien Clearance Desk for Title Agents
one_liner: A flat-fee curative service that proves dead solar fixture filings and other zombie liens are dead (or gets them released) so home closings stop stalling.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Residential solar leftovers: orphaned systems, leases and liens

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Per-file pain with a clear payer at closing, flat fee, easy free pilots with agencies. Make-or-break is underwriter acceptance of lapse memos.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lapse is not death; underwriters may reject memos; unauthorized-practice-of-law exposure.
judges.note: Zombie-lien proof-of-death is a real title pain, but lapse does not clear leases, debtor-filed terminations are narrow, and underwriters may refuse memos.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lapse isn't extinguishment; underwriters may not rely on memos; per-county ops-heavy.
judges.note: Real pain from solar bankruptcies and quick to start with title agents. Per-file service, small volume, UPL exposure, and underwriter acceptance is make-or-break.

title: Bedside Coverage Recovery for Safety-Net Hospitals
one_liner: A pay-on-success desk that helps safety-net hospital financial counselors convert lapsed or presumptively covered patients into full Medicaid within the shrinking retroactive window, with informal-income evidence built over text message, paid a flat fee per approved case by the hospital's revenue cycle budget.
lineage: mutation of I0573 ('Medicaid Hours Wallet for Gig Workers'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Benefit-rule changes: Medicaid work rules, SNAP and ACA cliffs

judges.fatal_flaw: Existing hospital Medicaid-eligibility outsourcers can add informal-income evidence; weak defensibility.
judges.note: Hard January 2027 retro-coverage cut makes speed a priced variable and pay-on-approval removes buyer risk, but it's a services wedge into an entrenched field.

judges.fatal_flaw: Existing hospital Medicaid-eligibility outsourcers likely already sell pay-on-success enrollment; fee-structure rules.
judges.note: Dated Jan 2027 forcing event, large hospital budget, pay-on-success lowers the sales barrier. Informal-income niche is real but narrow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Entrenched eligibility outsourcers already do this; PHI, BAA and hospital IT slow sales.
judges.note: Real Jan 2027 deadline and pay-on-success is an easy yes. But entrenched hospital eligibility vendors already do contingency enrollment; informal-income wedge is narrow.

title: Data Act Broker for Equipment Owners
one_liner: File and operationalize EU Data Act data-access demands so independent service shops can finally read the diagnostics that elevator, heat-pump, forklift and tractor makers lock away.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: EU digital product laws for small connected-device makers

judges.fatal_flaw: Value depends on OEM compliance and uneven enforcement; shops can file requests themselves.
judges.note: Big prize if it works, but depends on OEM compliance and enforcement; shops can file requests themselves, so brokerage moat is only normalization.

judges.fatal_flaw: OEMs can stall; shops can file requests themselves; templates commoditize quickly.
judges.note: Industrializing a legal right nobody exercises is a true contrarian insight with 2025-26 anchors. Execution hinges on OEMs actually delivering data and weak EU enforcement.

judges.fatal_flaw: OEMs can stall or return junk; shops can file Article 5 requests themselves.
judges.note: Industrializing a legal right is non-consensus with a real normalized-data moat if OEMs comply; enforcement is uneven.

title: Keep-the-Amps: Electrical Carve-Out for Plant Liquidations
one_liner: A 3,000-dollar electrician-verified 'in-place value memo' sold to industrial liquidators, trustees' counsel and corporate closure teams, so the switchgear and transformers are carved out of the equipment auction and sold with the real estate as a powered shell.
lineage: mutation of I0820 ('Power Passport: Scoring Dead Factories on Amps, Permits'), type: sharpened
cluster: US machine shops and reshoring manufacturers

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny market, and auctioneers earn commission selling the gear you want carved out.
judges.note: Genuinely original insight that powered shells beat scrap gear, easy $3k price, startable. But ceiling is under $1M and buyer incentives conflict.

judges.fatal_flaw: Self-admitted not venture-scale; roughly $1M total annual market.
judges.note: Elegant insight that auctions destroy powered shells and fast first revenue, but a $3k memo for a few hundred plants is a niche practice.

judges.fatal_flaw: Liquidators lack incentive; roughly 200 plants a year, not venture-scale.
judges.note: Truly non-obvious: the auction itself destroys the scarce energized asset. Anchored in power scarcity and transformer lead times. Cheap, fast to sell, small prize.

title: Outside-In Product Security Ratings for Insurers and Buyers
one_liner: Invert the desk: instead of helping one maker meet the 24-hour clock, independently measure from the outside whether thousands of connected-product makers can, and how exposed their shipped firmware is, and sell the scores and accumulation data to insurers, fleet buyers and lenders.
lineage: mutation of I0374 ('Outsourced 24-Hour Vulnerability Reporting Desk (CRA)'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: EU digital product laws for small connected-device makers

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers don't yet pay for product ratings; defamation and unauthorized-access exposure.
judges.note: Inverting the CRA desk into outside-in product ratings for insurers is ambitious and measurable. Long data build, legal risk, and slow insurer buying hurt six-month feasibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers have no product-level rating demand yet; outside-in probing carries legal exposure.
judges.note: Security-ratings clone applied to products. Calibration data and firmware access take years. Insurer pilots are slow, and the legal risk is real.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers won't pay until scores demonstrably predict losses; legal exposure from probing.
judges.note: BitSight-for-products riding the CRA deadline, with accumulation data as the moat; slow insurer sales and defamation risk temper it.

title: Stability Mark: Verified-Stable Tower Registry
one_liner: Invert the idea: instead of screening buildings for sinking, certify the many towers that have been stable for 10-30 years with a satellite-verified public mark and lookup registry that agents, lenders and insurers can trust, later backed by a scoping guarantee.
lineage: mutation of I1289 ('Settlement Passports for Florida High-Rise Condos'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Novel environmental and infrastructure data from satellites and crowd-sensing

judges.fatal_flaw: Ground-motion certificate invites liability if a certified tower fails; PEs may refuse co-signing.
judges.note: Status-signaling registry with unraveling dynamic and cornered archive is interesting, but a satellite 'stable' mark implies soundness it cannot prove.

judges.fatal_flaw: No buyer or lender demands the mark; certifying stability carries liability.
judges.note: Status-signal unraveling is an interesting theory, but it needs adoption before it has value, boards are reluctant, and InSAR is copyable.

judges.fatal_flaw: Certifier liability if a marked tower later fails despite measurement-only wording.
judges.note: Inverting fear into a status mark, with an unraveling adoption dynamic, is clever. The sensor-history archive is hard to copy, but liability and board inertia bite.

title: Owner-Side Ordering: The Royalty Asymmetry Calculator
one_liner: An advice-only LINE tool that tells franchise convenience-store owners how many fresh items to order and when to mark them down, using the owner's own payoff instead of HQ's.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Small trade and service firms underpricing and leaking margin

judges.fatal_flaw: Seven's new contract narrows asymmetry; Japan-only market is small.
judges.note: Best raw insight in the batch: owner payoff versus HQ payoff. But a small, shrinking-asymmetry, single-country market limits the prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Japan-only, easy-to-copy calculator; owners fear HQ retaliation; new contracts erode asymmetry.
judges.note: Sharp newsvendor insight (owner 22% vs HQ 70% critical ratio) and cheap LINE-bot pilot; prize is small and Seven's 2027 contract shrinks the asymmetry.

judges.fatal_flaw: Franchise agreements may bar tools; owners fear HQ retaliation; new contract shrinks gap.
judges.note: Real payoff asymmetry across 55K stores with gain-share pricing, but legacy-contract window is finite and market access, language and retaliation risks are heavy.

title: Remote Second-RN for Rural Night Shifts
one_liner: A pool of remote nurses that acts as the recorded, independent second person on video for narcotic waste, blood checks and high-alert drug double-checks when a rural hospital has three nurses on at 3am.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Rural and underserved patients who cannot reach care

judges.fatal_flaw: Remote witness may not satisfy state pharmacy or nursing rules; clinical liability.
judges.note: Supplying the missing second nurse rather than detecting diversion is a sharp reframe. Hospital-by-hospital sales, regulatory ambiguity, and virtual-nursing vendors able to add it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hospital policy, state-board and DEA acceptance of remote witnesses; slow sales to critical access hospitals.
judges.note: Real, sharp pain and a clever 'supply the missing colleague' insight. But 24/7 RN staffing, liability, and long hospital sales cycles hurt six-month traction.

judges.fatal_flaw: Boards of pharmacy or nursing may reject remote video witnessing of waste.
judges.note: Supplying the missing night-shift second nurse is a sharp insight, but about 1,300 hospitals at $2k/month is a small, labor-heavy market.

title: Neutral Baselines and Neighbor Guarantees for Data Centers
one_liner: A neutral third party installs pre-construction sensors around proposed data centers and administers a developer-funded, automatic payout guarantee to neighbors, so permit fights run on evidence.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Localities, utilities and landowners facing speculative data-center demand

judges.fatal_flaw: Developers may refuse pre-committed payouts; attribution and insurance-law exposure.
judges.note: Social license is the choke point of the data-center buildout. A neutral baseline plus parametric guarantee could become a permit standard, and it generalizes to any contested siting.

judges.fatal_flaw: Sensor baseline layer is commoditizing (KETOS, Aethair); guarantee payout resembles unlicensed insurance.
judges.note: Parametric neighbor payout is interesting but sold on top of a crowded sensor business. The sharpened M1 version dominates this original.

judges.fatal_flaw: Attribution disputes and insurance-law exposure on automatic payouts; commoditizing sensors.
judges.note: Developers need hearing evidence now and a pilot is cheap, but KETOS and Aethair already sell baselines; guarantee escrow adds regulatory baggage.

title: Rural Sales Commons: Pay Retiring Appraisers for Comps
one_liner: Invert the idea: instead of retirees paying to leave, pay them for their verified sales books and build the private sales-price registry that non-disclosure states lack, sold first to practicing rural appraisers and later to AVM, lender and assessor buyers.
lineage: mutation of I1039 ('Retirement-in-a-Box for Exiting Appraisers'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Owner wind-down, sudden death and tacit-knowledge handoff

judges.fatal_flaw: MLS license, USPAP confidentiality and GLBA exposure may void the data set.
judges.note: Dying comp books are a real cornered resource, but $39-59 subscriptions are small, data-licence demand is unvalidated, legal gating comes first.

judges.fatal_flaw: Comp books likely entangled with MLS licenses and client confidentiality; unlicensable data.
judges.note: Cornered-resource angle on retiring appraisers' sales books is original; legal data-rights risk could invalidate the asset.

judges.fatal_flaw: MLS, USPAP and GLBA legal risk may gut the extractable dataset.
judges.note: Retirees as suppliers with a ticking clock is a good cornered-resource inversion. Willingness to pay and legality are unproven, and subscriptions are small.

title: Ship-Date Cliff Audits for Phased Campuses
one_liner: A fixed-fee clock-map, rider-negotiation and proof-test sprint for developers of multi-phase data center campuses whose pre-bought gensets, UPS and chillers were shipped long before the halls they serve, so the OEM 18-months-from-ship outer limit expires before startup.
lineage: mutation of I0229 ('Warranty Clock Recovery Audits for Idle Halls'), type: sharpened
cluster: Warranty claims left unfiled

judges.fatal_flaw: Warranty exposure narrow; OEMs can dispute claims; extraction is commodity.
judges.note: Provable from shipment documents and campus-wide order leverage is smart. Exposure is narrower than the pitch and mostly consulting-sized.

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: High-ACV fixed-fee wedge reachable via public air permits; countable outcomes (signed deferral, credit memo). Exposure narrower than parent and prize about $2M ARR.

judges.fatal_flaw: Procurement can ask the OEM for deferral riders directly; exposure is narrow.
judges.note: Document-provable exposure (ship date vs startup) is smart, but the competitor check itself shrank the problem. Services only, small repeat base.

title: Chute-Side Cow Counts for Ag Lenders
one_liner: Turn the vet's preg-check clipboard into a borrower-consented, third-party-verified herd inventory that banks can lend against.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Lenders and investors unable to verify collateral exists

judges.fatal_flaw: Borrower-initiated counts adversely select honest ranchers; revenue per head is tiny.
judges.note: Vet is the only independent hand on every animal and a lender-mandated covenant is credible, but prize is small and community banks adopt slowly.

judges.fatal_flaw: Adverse selection: fraudsters won't opt in; chute count proves neither ownership nor lien.
judges.note: Vet is the only independent party touching every cow; fraud case and record prices give timing. Tangible and pilotable now, but small per-head revenue and vendor entry risk.

judges.fatal_flaw: $2-3/head, split with vets; borrower-initiated checks miss the fraudsters.
judges.note: Genuine lender pain and a clever vet-as-witness insight. Revenue per borrower is ~$1k, vets may refuse, and the lender sales cycle is slow.

title: Dark Roof Capital: Buy, Cure, Re-Perform
one_liner: Invert the parent. Instead of being paid a $3k fee to cure other people's stranded solar loans, buy those loans at dark-roof prices, finish the systems with a proprietary per-AHJ cure playbook, and keep the full value uplift as a re-performing loan pool.
lineage: mutation of I1175 ('Finish Crew: Stranded Solar Job Completion'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Residential solar leftovers: orphaned systems, leases and liens

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs balance sheet, servicer licensing; borrower reinstatement and rescission unproven
judges.note: Owning the asset captures the cure uplift fee-for-service misses; real stranded-loan pool. Capital, licensing, Holder Rule and borrower-reinstatement risks are heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Capital-intensive; consumer-lending licensing and FTC Holder Rule liability exceed a scrappy team.
judges.note: Inverting from fee to ownership captures the cure uplift, contrarian and well-timed after installer bankruptcies, but needs balance sheet and the cure-share phase is thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs distressed-loan capital, lender licences, Holder Rule and rescission exposure.
judges.note: Inversion captures more value, but capital, servicing licences and borrower reinstatement risk before revenue. Phase 1 cure-share is just a weaker M1.

title: Independent Auditor for AI-Paid Pet Claims
one_liner: A read-only shadow adjudicator plus a cross-carrier duplicate registry that independently re-checks every auto-paid pet claim against the policy's own clauses and produces the validation records state examiners now ask for.
lineage: mutation of I1056 ('Unbundling Edits for Pet Insurance Claims'), type: sharpened
cluster: Pet owners and insurers squeezed by rising vet bills

judges.fatal_flaw: Only dozens of pet MGAs; tiny prize unless extended beyond pet.
judges.note: Independent audit of AI-paid claims with regulator pull (NAIC bulletin) and a hashed duplicate registry is smart. Pet is a thin wedge; the real company is cross-line AI claims validation.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers; vendors and carriers can add audit modules; AI-compliance category crowded.
judges.note: Independence from the automating vendor is a real insight and the hashed duplicate registry is neat. Tiny pet-insurer universe caps the prize and sits near the AI-audit pattern.

judges.fatal_flaw: Only dozens of pet carriers and MGAs; slow insurer sales; registry cold start.
judges.note: Independence-as-product and NAIC bulletin hook are sharp, but tiny buyer pool and the AI-claims-audit framing is crowded.

title: Contingency Recovery for Contaminated Survey Sample
one_liner: A freight-audit-style recovery firm that finds contaminated and duplicated completes in the survey sample buyers already paid for, files credit claims against panel vendors, and keeps 25-35% of what it recovers.
lineage: mutation of I0716 ('Independent Referee for Survey Panel Data'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Gatekeepers drowning in AI-generated submissions and bot responses

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Freight-audit model on a new category: zero-upfront offer, finance buyer. Risk: vendor remedies may be credits or replacement sample, making fees hard to collect.

judges.fatal_flaw: Sample MSAs rarely include refundable quality SLAs; agencies won't claim against vendors they depend on.
judges.note: Reframing quality as receivables moves the buyer to finance, which is smart. Dispute dynamics and modest per-customer yield limit it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Agencies unlikely to sue their own panel suppliers; claims hinge on SLA clauses.
judges.note: Reframing quality as accounts receivable is clever, but low ticket ($22-45k), vendor relationships and an AI-pressured research industry make recovery unlikely.

title: Neutral Registry and Standard for Neighbor Baselines
one_liner: An independent, vendor-agnostic registry and open protocol that notarizes pre-construction baselines from any sensor vendor or consultant, gets referenced in county ordinances and a model presumption statute, and becomes the title-plant-style record that insurers and lenders underwrite against.
lineage: mutation of I1172 ('Neutral Baselines and Neighbor Guarantees for Data Centers'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Localities, utilities and landowners facing speculative data-center demand

judges.fatal_flaw: No legal mandate to buy a registry filing; adoption depends on slow ordinances and legislation.
judges.note: Neutral notary for tamper-evident baselines sits on top of data-center backlash; incumbents become channel. Huge upside if one county or statute names it.

judges.fatal_flaw: No legal mandate to buy; depends on ordinances and legislation within months.
judges.note: Timely moratorium backlash and an auditor-style neutral stamp, but this is a regulatory-adoption bet. Developers pay only if counties require it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Revenue gated on ordinances and presumption statutes adopted by counties and legislatures.
judges.note: Standard-and-registry play needs regulatory adoption before real demand; parent already lets developers buy baselines directly, so this is a step backward.

title: Private Road Associations in a Box
one_liner: Turn the neighbors' informal, cash-in-a-coffee-can road fund into a recorded, insurable road association with dues, reserves and competitively bid plowing and grading.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Home closings, condo boards and HOAs tangled in title and records rules

judges.fatal_flaw: Not venture-scale; PayHOA cheap; lien enforcement and dues float state-dependent.
judges.note: Closing-triggered distribution through attorneys and title agents is clever and gets first customers fast. Likely a solid regional business, not a giant.

judges.fatal_flaw: Unauthorized-practice-of-law exposure; state-by-state drafting; modest total market.
judges.note: Closing-triggered urgency and attorney referrals make first customers easy; boring and unserved. Weak why-now and limited scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: $12-25 per household admin versus PayHOA at $2; state-specific legal and trust rules.
judges.note: Stalled-closing urgency via attorneys is a real channel and first sales plausible, but few deals per attorney and recurring admin does not hold.

title: Tele-Clearance for Sheriffs' Booking Desks
one_liner: A night-shift nurse-and-NP screening service that lets a rural deputy clear an arrestee for booking from the jail, without spending four hours in the ER while the county goes unpatrolled.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Rural sheriffs, jails and small police agencies

judges.fatal_flaw: Remote clearance shifts malpractice liability to vendor; cross-state NP licensing unresolved.
judges.note: Deputy-hours-returned framing is a sharp insight and county risk pools pay. Revenue is thin (12 counties about $300-500k) and liability heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Remote clearance shifts clinical liability to vendor; slow county sales; NP licensing per state.
judges.note: $85 screen versus $2-4k ER trip plus stranded deputy is an obvious budgeted ROI; risk pools can fund; revenue ceiling modest.

judges.fatal_flaw: Remote clearance shifts malpractice liability; NPs need per-state licenses; thin county revenue.
judges.note: The deputy-hours insight is real and well observed. Revenue ceiling is roughly $0.5M for 12 counties, with slow sales and liability the risk pool may reject.

title: Fees-in-Kind: Harvest Becomes School Fee Credit
one_liner: A weigh-in and ledger service that lets parents pay school fees with maize, beans and potatoes at a transparent price, while schools get cheaper, steadier food supply.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Smallholders and rural households in emerging markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Low defensibility; collector-plus-supplier conflict of interest; 2026 maize shortage.
judges.note: Genuinely out-of-the-box: formalizes the barter parents already use, with trust ledger. Scrappy pilot in weeks; prize and defensibility are modest, maize shortage hurts.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin 4-8% commodity margin, conflict of interest, small day-school tickets, slow tenders.
judges.note: Genuine local insight into barter-as-payment and trust ledgers. Weak unit economics, maize-shortage year, and a procurement piece that likely fails.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low-margin commodity logistics with grain working capital and slow-paying school buyers.
judges.note: Genuine rural Kenyan pain and clever ledger, but 4-8% margin, 2026 maize shortage, tender kickbacks, and a remote team operating physical supply chains.

title: Pharmacy-Side PBM Ledger for Employers
one_liner: Independent pharmacies hold the half of the PBM ledger that employers never see, which is what the PBM actually paid the pharmacy. Pool it to run spread audits for self-insured employers, and give pharmacies a stay-or-leave calculator for their take-it-or-leave-it PBM contracts.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Independent pharmacies squeezed by PBMs, refund floats and deserts

judges.fatal_flaw: Cold-start pooling, PBM confidentiality clauses, antitrust; cannot be built before January.
judges.note: Two-sided data pooling with employers is the harder, riskier version; confidentiality, antitrust, and the January window undermine it. Mutation M1 is better.

judges.fatal_flaw: Pooling pharmacy reimbursement data hits PBM confidentiality clauses and antitrust risk.
judges.note: Pharmacy-side remits are the genuinely missing half of the PBM ledger. Huge spend, pooled-data moat, cheap pharmacy wedge. Legal structure is the real work.

judges.fatal_flaw: Pharmacies pay little; two-sided cold start; data confidentiality; January window unreachable.
judges.note: Pharmacy-side data insight is good but the $99/month pharmacy side is weak and PSAOs may already hold it. M2 mutation is stronger.

title: Medicaid Hours Wallet for Gig Workers
one_liner: A phone-based monthly proof-of-work ledger that turns gig, cash and self-employment activity into state-accepted documentation and 30-day cure packets, paid for by the Medicaid plans and health centers that lose revenue when members drop.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Benefit-rule changes: Medicaid work rules, SNAP and ACA cliffs

judges.fatal_flaw: MCO buyers procure slowly and are limited to support role; enrollees must self-adopt.
judges.note: Urgent deadline, but wrong buyer: MCOs are slow and capped at a support role. Cure Desk mutation fixes this.

judges.fatal_flaw: IFR limits plans to assisting only; state verification tools may make a separate packet redundant.
judges.note: Hard Jan 2027 deadline and MCOs/FQHCs with real revenue at stake; enrollee-side documentation for gig and cash work is unaddressed; policy risk high.

judges.fatal_flaw: MCOs are a weak buyer; state consent-based verification tools make it redundant.
judges.note: Real Jan 2027 deadline and lopsided retention math, but plans cannot determine compliance and the policy is politically fragile.

title: Mother-Tongue Lifeline for Dementia Flashpoints
one_liner: On-demand live video calls where a dementia-trained speaker of the patient's first language and dialect coaches the English-speaking aide and calms the patient at bath, bedtime and exit-seeking moments.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Dementia and Alzheimer's care at home and in memory care

judges.fatal_flaw: Agencies cannot bill Medicaid for it; AI dialect translation may displace.
judges.note: Original, emotionally true, cheap supply of bilingual retirees. Startable on WhatsApp, but willingness to pay and AI voice substitutes cap the prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Home care agencies on thin Medicaid margins may not pay per minute; dialect-supply liquidity.
judges.note: Genuinely human insight: validate and calm in the childhood dialect, not translate. Pilotable fast with one agency; payer and 24/7 long-tail supply are unresolved.

judges.fatal_flaw: Agencies run thin margins; no Medicaid code pays; on-demand dialect supply liquidity.
judges.note: Sharp insight on dialect reversion and cheap to pilot over WhatsApp. But small per-minute revenue, spiky supply, and interpreter vendors can bolt on.

title: Bench-Truth Diligence for Biotech Investors
one_liner: Sell seed VCs, pharma BD teams and AI-bio founders confidential 'does this paper's key result actually work?' intelligence, from anonymous postdoc consensus polls up to paid replication of the one key experiment.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Biotech capital: diligence and salvage

judges.fatal_flaw: Anonymity leaks in small subfields; postdoc confidentiality and defamation exposure; GLG can copy.
judges.note: Focused poll-first wedge, fund budgets exist, quick $5k pilot; replication ambiguity and legal exposure limit trust.

judges.fatal_flaw: Anonymity leaks in small subfields; postdoc confidentiality and defamation exposure; GLG can copy.
judges.note: Right insight: candid junior-bench consensus beats conflicted KOL calls; cheap to start, $5k polls. Small market and weak why-now beyond layoffs.

judges.fatal_flaw: GLG can copy the poll cheaply; anonymity leaks in small subfields; defamation exposure.
judges.note: Candid junior-postdoc consensus is a real wedge and cheap to test. The market is small and the replication upsell is unreliable.

title: AI Chat-History Exposure Assessments for Breach Counsel
one_liner: When infostealers grab employees' AI sessions, tell breach counsel what the attacker could actually have read and whether notification is triggered.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Recorded and AI-created data exposure for small firms

judges.fatal_flaw: Provider-side session-access logs unobtainable; cannot prove what attacker actually read.
judges.note: Notification law turns on data, not credentials: sharp reframing with real incident volume. Sold through IR boutiques, but proof gap and easy copying cap it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Stolen cookie doesn't prove chats were read; needs provider logs only tenants hold.
judges.note: Counsel-facing deliverable is a real gap, but incidents are lumpy, feed licences cost, and first ten paid assessments in six months is unlikely.

judges.fatal_flaw: A stolen cookie does not prove chats were read; needs provider logs held by others.
judges.note: Fresh category with breach counsel as an unusual buyer. Thin data access and infostealer vendors can add the memo as a services line.

title: Day-Zero Payoff Bridge for Floorplan Dealers
one_liner: Invert the radar: instead of catching dealers who fail to pay the floorplan lender, wire the payoff directly to the lender the day the car sells and get repaid when the retail contract funds, turning sold-out-of-trust risk into a short, fully secured receivable with data-driven underwriting.
lineage: mutation of I0218 ('Sold-Out-of-Trust Radar for Floorplan Lenders'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Lenders and investors unable to verify collateral exists

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs credit-fund capital and lending licenses; contract-in-transit financing incumbents unchecked.
judges.note: Clever inversion of detection into secured short-term credit; big prize but capital-heavy, licensed, and thin net margins versus dealer working-capital lines.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs credit facility and state lending licenses before meaningful revenue.
judges.note: Capital-heavy bridge lending with dilution risk and two-sided trust; highest variance in the batch; bootstrapped team cannot start.

judges.fatal_flaw: Adverse selection, licensing, and capital needs; NextGear/Cox can undercut.
judges.note: Reframing sold-out-of-trust as a timing gap is sharp, but it is a capital-heavy lending business with adverse selection and state licensing.

title: Recall Drills: State QC Findings Become Worker Training
one_liner: A recall-notice system for SNAP errors: every finding from a state's own QC review and every H.R.1 rule change becomes a dollar-tagged synthetic drill within 14 days, delivered through the state's CQI field staff to new hires in its highest-error counties, with an audit trail for corrective-action plans.
lineage: mutation of I1240 ('Flight simulator drills for county SNAP eligibility workers'), type: sharpened
cluster: Benefit-rule changes: Medicaid work rules, SNAP and ACA cliffs

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow state procurement; ceiling around $10-20M ARR; needs QC data-sharing agreement.
judges.note: Hard financial driver (H.R.1 error cost-share) and clever recall-loop framing, but state procurement is slow and the author's own ceiling is $10-20M ARR.

judges.fatal_flaw: State training budgets and data-sharing MOUs mean slow sales; county-level buyers lack money.
judges.note: Dollar-tagged recall loop is clever, but training is a weaker buyer than system testing; $10-20M ceiling and slow government sales.

judges.fatal_flaw: State procurement cycles; Maximus-type vendors can bundle training; modest roughly $10-20M ceiling.
judges.note: Deadline-driven by H.R.1 error-rate cost shares; recall loop on states' own QC findings is a smart data position, but small, slow government buyers.

title: Cross-Mine Critical Spares Pool and Inventory Cleanup
one_liner: An AI cleaner for mine SAP materials masters that frees cash from duplicate spares, then turns the informal WhatsApp groups of competing mines' maintenance planners into a contractual, insured rotables pool for mill motors, liners and haul-truck parts.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Singular / uncategorized

judges.fatal_flaw: Step one is commoditized; pooling competitors raises antitrust exposure.

judges.fatal_flaw: Competing mines must share data; antitrust exposure; OEM reman programs substitute.
judges.note: Aviation-style rotable pooling for mining is non-consensus and huge if it works; step one is crowded by Verusen.

judges.fatal_flaw: Step one crowded (Verusen); pooling events rare; competitor data-sharing antitrust exposure.
judges.note: The WhatsApp swap network as the real supply chain is a sharp insight, but the saleable wedge is crowded and the pooling product needs slow trust-building.

title: Implant Payment Index for ASC Networks
one_liner: Pool invoice-versus-payment data across physician-owned ASC networks to build the payer-by-procedure benchmark that only payers hold today, and turn it into the reference price index that carve-out contracts cite instead of each ASC's own invoice.
lineage: mutation of I0708 ('Contingency Recovery of Unpaid Implant Carve-Outs'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Provider revenue leaks and payer denials

judges.fatal_flaw: Data-pooling cold start and antitrust exposure; payers must adopt index.
judges.note: Neutral implant reference index could end invoice-attachment fights; ratio-only design is clever. Pooling cold start, antitrust, and PHI make it a slow standard-setting bet.

judges.fatal_flaw: Antitrust exposure from pooling payment data across competing ASCs; small market.
judges.note: Index-as-contract-reference logic is good, and the ratio design is clever. About 1,000 buyers, payer adoption uncertain, and carve-outs are commercial-only.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cold-start data pooling among competing ASCs with antitrust exposure; weaker than parent.
judges.note: Clever neutral-index idea, but slower to first dollar than direct recovery. MSO buyers are concentrated and payers hold the real data.

title: Placement Proof for Workforce Pell Providers
one_liner: A verified job-placement and completion ledger that makes short-term training programs (CDL, CNA, welding, HVAC, medical assistant, cosmetology) audit-ready for the governor and Secretary approvals that Workforce Pell requires.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Colleges and training programs under new federal loan caps and earnings tests

judges.fatal_flaw: States may verify via UI wage records; SIS vendors can bolt it on
judges.note: Deadline-driven by Workforce Pell's 12-month look-back, real compliance pain. But small buyer count and SIS vendors or state wage-record matching can erase it.

judges.fatal_flaw: State wage-record matching or SIS vendors may absorb it; few approved programs initially.
judges.note: Real deadline-driven pain with 12-month look-back and small-school budgets; competitor check was weak; buyer count starts small.

judges.fatal_flaw: States may verify placement from wage records; SIS vendors can bolt this on.
judges.note: Regulation-driven evidence gap with a real clock, but a thin buyer pool at first, low defensibility, and an obvious feature for student-information-system vendors.

title: Lender-Paid Calf Collateral Inspection and Lot Grading
one_liner: Sell independent day-3-to-6 lot grading to the feed, milk-replacer and ag-loan credit desks that finance calf raisers, as collateral inspection, so the party who really loses money on every dead calf pays for the measurement.
lineage: mutation of I0617 ('Immune-Graded Beef-on-Dairy Calves With Warranty'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Farm and ranch risks: disease, cash, storage and machinery

judges.fatal_flaw: Small market; loss figures unverified; lenders may not pay inspection fees.
judges.note: Moving the payer to the credit desk is a good inversion of the parent. The beef-on-dairy collateral niche is small and unvalidated.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lenders may not name bad-debt numbers; few distributor buyers, small market.
judges.note: Clever reframing: the credit desk bears calf risk. Cheap field inspection, clear kill gate. Niche, slow, and loss-rate evidence is unverified.

judges.fatal_flaw: Passive-transfer failure is only one loss driver; lenders may not price it.
judges.note: Flips the payer to the credit provider holding the loss. Beef-on-dairy calf values are a real shift. Niche, field-service heavy, modest fees.

title: Payable Bias Audit for Black Mass Sellers
one_liner: A fixed-price audit that measures, in euros per year, the systematic sampling bias between a black mass seller's protocol and its buyer's. The fix is then locked in as a sealed sample-of-record and a two-line contract clause.
lineage: mutation of I1326 ('Referee Sampling for Black Mass and Battery Scrap'), type: sharpened
cluster: Recycling quality, distressed capacity and battery/EPR compliance

judges.fatal_flaw: Only ~50 sellers in corridor; services niche majors could undercut.
judges.note: Sharp insight: systematic bias, not noise, costs sellers euros, and the majors face channel conflict. Prize is a small specialist service.

judges.fatal_flaw: Only 40-60 sellers in corridor; SGS, Intertek or Bureau Veritas could copy.
judges.note: Systematic bias, not noise, is the non-obvious insight; euro-quantified free historical-pair test makes outbound sales concrete. Prize is small and niche.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny seller universe; needs Theory-of-Sampling expertise the team lacks.
judges.note: Euro-denominated bias pitch is sharp and outbound-friendly, but only 40-60 prospects, Europe-based, lab-dependent and majors can respond.

title: Independent Herd Audits for Loan Participation Buyers
one_liner: Charge the correspondent banks, credit unions and credit funds that buy pieces of cattle loans they cannot see, using sampling audits and a verified collateral tape sold through bankers' banks.
lineage: mutation of I0338 ('Chute-Side Cow Counts for Ag Lenders'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Lenders and investors unable to verify collateral exists

judges.fatal_flaw: Small niche market, about $1.5M for ten buyers; fraud detection needs lead-bank cooperation.
judges.note: Selling audits to the blind buyer of risk, not the originator, is a real insight; tiny, concentrated market and lead-bank cooperation limit scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny market; participants have ignored inspection rights for years.
judges.note: Selling to the risk-buyer is the right inversion, but cattle participations are niche: about $1.5M ARR at ten buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers never exercise inspection rights today; bank vendor onboarding is slow.
judges.note: Independence insight is sound, but no budget line exists and bankers-bank channel is unproven. Fraud premise unverified; economics overstated.

title: Aftermarket Support for Stranded DJI Fleets
one_liner: Repair, rebuilt batteries, parts and firmware-independence retrofits for the many legally owned DJI drones that can no longer be replaced with new models.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Aircraft and drone operators: maintenance, parts, permits and navigation

judges.fatal_flaw: DJI/CarePro and Drone Nerds already repair; DJI parts access and battery lockouts cap moat.
judges.note: Serving the stranded installed base is sensible and easy to start, but it is commodity repair with no moat and incumbents already serve it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Parts supply from China is throttled; DJI and existing repairers already compete.
judges.note: Real repair backlog (months), urgent budgeted public-safety and ag buyers, instantly startable bench and SLA depot. Easiest first ten customers; defensibility thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: DJI controls parts and batteries; retroactive FCC action could erase the fleets.
judges.note: Strong why-now but not unserved: DJI, Drone Nerds and others repair. Depot services with a shrinking asset base and no venture-scale moat.

title: Vet-Verified Herd Exposure and Outbreak Index
one_liner: Rural large-animal vets sell two things from one app: borrower-approved, chute-side verified herd counts for ag lenders, and anonymized weekly syndrome tallies whose denominators come from those counts, giving lenders, insurers and traders a true disease-rate signal.

cluster: Lenders and investors unable to verify collateral exists

judges.fatal_flaw: Lender verification suffers adverse selection and risks vets' trusted-advisor position.
judges.note: Hybrid is genuinely stronger: denominators fix the outbreak index and vets earn twice. Exposure plus hazard data targets livestock insurers, but two buyers add complexity.

judges.fatal_flaw: Adverse selection; vets refuse to police clients; government reporting substitutes.
judges.note: Bundling two vet-dependent products compounds risk: borrower-initiated audits suffer adverse selection, and selling outbreak signals to funds raises MNPI concerns.

judges.fatal_flaw: Two cold-start data products; adverse selection; selling outbreak signals raises MNPI issues.
judges.note: Hybrid is bigger, not stronger: vets must log heads and file tallies for thin pay. Free government alternatives exist.

title: Interim Smoke-Damage Protocol Before the State Standard

judges.fatal_flaw: Advantage evaporates when DTSC standards land; crowded CIH assessors; carriers resist.
judges.note: Sharp 2027 compliance window and a protocol-as-standard play, but it is CA-specific, services-heavy, and a buyer-conflict mess between carriers and policyholders.

judges.fatal_flaw: Assessment supply crowded; carriers conflicted buyers; technician network capital heavy.

title: Human Bench Network for AI Agents
