judges.fatal_flaw: A CRO with an API; Adaptyv or Scientist.com can copy; margins unproven
judges.note: Genuine bottleneck with frontier-lab evidence, fast to first pilots. Margins, contamination liability and Adaptyv or CRO marketplaces adding agent APIs threaten defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Sublet-bench liability, contamination and QC risk; margins unproven against commodity CROs.
judges.note: Real bench bottleneck, but wet-lab operations are heavy and Adaptyv or Scientist.com can add agent APIs; 'humans for agents' framing is trendy.

judges.fatal_flaw: CROs and Adaptyv can add an agent API; liability and margin unproven.
judges.note: Humans as last-mile actuators for AI agents is topical, but the 'humans for AI' trope is crowded and the layoff supply story is weakening.

title: Sold-Out-of-Trust Radar for Floorplan Lenders
one_liner: Catch dealers that sell floored cars and pocket the payoff by watching the one signal an F&I insider knows can't be hidden: the VIN disappears from public listings but the floorplan payoff never arrives.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Lenders and investors unable to verify collateral exists

judges.fatal_flaw: Noisy signal, fixed windows, unvalidated pricing; superseded by its sharpened mutation.
judges.note: Original radar is closer to a feature; the M1 mutation fixes its flaws, so this version adds nothing beyond it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Disappearing-listing signal is noisy; scraping terms risk; lenders can build in-house.
judges.note: Insider insight, urgent fraud pain, small lenders reachable via free pilot with backtest on public cases. Modest prize, thin defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Delisting is a noisy signal; lenders can build it in-house; small niche.
judges.note: The 'what left the internet' insight is clever but raw. The mutation I0218-M1 fixes its noise and dispatch problems and dominates it.

title: Contingency Recovery of Missed Rotable Repair Warranties
one_liner: A success-fee auditor that finds repaired aircraft components that failed inside the shop's warranty window, and turns them into filed claims and cash.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Warranty claims left unfiled

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny addressable market; shop warranty exclusions; getting AP and maintenance exports is hard.
judges.note: Freight-audit playbook for aviation rotables is sensible and cheap to try. Niche is small, moat thin, and evidence rests on homepage silence.

judges.fatal_flaw: Operators fear antagonizing shops; power-by-the-hour contracts erase many claims; small TAM.
judges.note: Zero-upfront contingency is an easy yes and the audit playbook is proven; AP-to-maintenance join is the real insight. Small TAM and shop relationships limit scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Power-by-the-hour contracts remove warranty exposure; small-operator data exports are hard.
judges.note: Classic freight-audit playbook in a niche. Real leak, but weak why-now beyond LLM invoice parsing and a small addressable base.

title: Pooled Calendar Reporters for Limited-Scope Family Lawyers
one_liner: One physically present reporter sits an entire family-court calendar and sells the record by the matter, about $110 per 15-minute hearing, so each lawyer pays roughly 75% less than a half-day pro tem while the reporter earns more than a normal pro tem day.
lineage: mutation of I0248 ('Fifteen-Minute Court Reporting for Family Law Hearings'), type: sharpened
cluster: Small litigation practices lacking evidence, records and benchmark tools

judges.fatal_flaw: Court rules, unions and confidentiality may block pooled private reporters; weak moat.
judges.note: Crowdfunded-threshold calendar coverage fixes the dead-time problem and is runnable in 30 days. Real post-ruling demand, but easily copied and legally untested.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small prize: about $700 platform margin per reporter-day; court permission for shared private reporter unverified.
judges.note: Lawful in-person redesign of a barred remote idea; threshold booking is clever. Two-sided cold start per courthouse and tiny margins limit scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small thin-margin staffing business; reporter unions and court rules limit scale.
judges.note: Concrete pay-per-matter model launches on a spreadsheet and sidesteps the remote ban, but it is a reporter-staffing service.

title: Real-Factory Credentials From Customs Shipping Records
one_liner: Turn public US import records into supplier-owned reputation credentials and audit-ready reasonable-care dossiers that prove a factory is a real manufacturer.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Brands substantiating origin, recycled-content and green claims

judges.fatal_flaw: ImportGenius already sells supplier verification at same price; records often name forwarders, not factories.
judges.note: Strong why-now in transshipment enforcement, but the wedge is thin: data incumbents can add a risk report, and the factory-pays credential is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: ImportGenius already sells supplier verification; records often name forwarders, not factories.
judges.note: Strong why-now (transshipment liability) and large prize, but the SMB wedge is thin and enterprise tools can bolt it on.

judges.fatal_flaw: Customs data often names forwarders; ImportGenius already sells supplier verification.
judges.note: Tariff timing is real, but the dossier is thin over cheap data, incumbents add it quickly, and the factory-pays credential has no demand.

title: Daubert-Ready Sample Audits for Litigation Surveys
one_liner: A neutral data-quality auditor that gives survey experts and litigators a signed, control-calibrated audit of the respondent sample behind a Lanham Act, false-advertising or damages survey, or a teardown of the other side's sample.
lineage: mutation of I0716 ('Independent Referee for Survey Panel Data'), type: sharpened
cluster: Gatekeepers drowning in AI-generated submissions and bot responses

judges.fatal_flaw: Only 30-60 testifying-expert buyers; tiny addressable market.
judges.note: Litigation-budget insensitivity is a good insight and the price is high. Prize is small and needs licensed control panels plus a testifying methodologist.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer pool; lumpy case-driven demand; experts reluctant to expose own samples.
judges.note: High per-case willingness to pay and timely bot problem, but 30-60 expert buyers and need for panel licensing plus academic testifier.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer pool; needs licensed control panel and a testifying academic methodologist.
judges.note: Insurance-against-cross-examination is a sound willingness-to-pay insight, and bots biasing net effects is clever. Market is a few dozen experts.

title: Neutral Monitoring That Unlocks Backup Diesel Dispatch
one_liner: A permit-to-dispatch package for data center backup generators that bundles neutral fence-line and neighbor-home monitoring with an automatic neighbor payout guarantee, so regulators and neighbors can say yes to more run-hours.
lineage: hybrid of I1172 + I0836 (Neutral Baselines and Neighbor Guarantees for Data Centers + Air-Permit Unlock for Idle Data Center Diesel). Why stronger: The permit playbook alone has long enterprise cycles and depends on regulators trusting the operator. The monitoring business alone competes with KETOS-style sensor vendors and is a cost center for developers. Combined, the monitoring is the missing permission-to-operate evidence, and the permit unlock gives the monitoring a clear ROI, a percentage-of-capacity-revenue upside, and a repeatable per-state playbook that is hard to copy.
cluster: Localities, utilities and landowners facing speculative data-center demand

judges.fatal_flaw: Emergency-engine rules bar capacity income without costly reclassification and retrofits.
judges.note: Huge prize if capacity revenue unlocks, and the permission-to-operate framing is original; two businesses glued together with long enterprise cycles.

judges.fatal_flaw: 40 CFR 63.6640(f) bars selling emergency-engine hours; retrofit and permit fights precede revenue.
judges.note: Four businesses stapled together: permitting, sensors, escrow payouts and PJM enrollment. Enterprise cycles, regulator dependence and possible insurance-law issues sink a scrappy start.

judges.fatal_flaw: Emergency-engine rules bar capacity income without costly reclassification and retrofit.
judges.note: Neighbor-payout guarantee is creative, but the data-center energy theme is crowded, permit cycles are long, and the legal constraint likely kills the economics.

title: Solar Job Escrow: Bankruptcy-Proof Project Records
one_liner: A neutral escrow that captures every financed solar job's permit, design, serial and step-in authorizations before the installer fails. The installer pays per job, the lender enforces deposits through milestone funding, and cure is paid from the final milestone the lender is still holding.
lineage: mutation of I1175 ('Finish Crew: Stranded Solar Job Completion'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Residential solar leftovers: orphaned systems, leases and liens

judges.fatal_flaw: Requires lenders to change funding conditions; loan-financed solar volume is shrinking after 25D ended.
judges.note: Sharp insight: the lender already holds the cure budget (final milestone) and controls deposits. Strong pre-failure positioning, but installer CRMs and lenders could build it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs lenders to change funding conditions; residential solar market is contracting.
judges.note: Lender-enforced escrow is a good mechanism and answers the parent's lumpiness. Per-job fees cap the prize in a shrinking market.

judges.fatal_flaw: Requires lenders to change funding conditions; failing installers won't pay.
judges.note: Milestone-funding enforcement is a smart hook, but solar installers are collapsing, lenders are slow gatekeepers, and the payer is not the protected party.

title: Independent Audit Samples for Modeled Lead Inventories
one_liner: Become the independent auditor of predictive lead-line inventories: sell engineering consultants and state reviewers a statistically designed sample of 60-150 photo-verified lines that proves a model's error rate, paid per ground-truth point plus an annual attestation fee.
lineage: mutation of I0463 ('Pay Home Inspectors to Find Lead Pipes'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Small water utilities: staffing, revenue leakage, lead lines and nitrate

judges.fatal_flaw: States may require water-system personnel verification; small niche market
judges.note: Sampling math makes the audit small and credible; independence is the product. Narrow niche, few buyers, states may not accept third-party photo evidence.

judges.fatal_flaw: No regulator requires audit samples; consultants avoid paying to expose their model's errors.
judges.note: Sampling math is smart and buyers have contract vehicles. But no regulator demands audits and consultants have no incentive to expose their own model error.

judges.fatal_flaw: States may require water-system personnel verification; tiny per-utility revenue.
judges.note: Sample-not-census statistics is genuinely right and removes the response-rate problem. Regulatory acceptance and federal rule uncertainty cap the size.

title: Mzee's Testament: Family Land Councils Before Death
one_liner: Invert the parent: instead of untangling the dead man's land after the funeral, hold a video-witnessed Family Land Council this December while the parent is alive and every heir is home, lock it into a will, family agreement, capacity certificate and time-locked vault, and grow the format into a registry of family land intent.
lineage: mutation of I0474 ('Dead Capital: Succession Kits for Diaspora Families'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Diaspora families managing death, care and property across borders

judges.fatal_flaw: About $310 ticket, heavy legal liability, Kenya-specific ops; tiny first-year revenue.
judges.note: Inversion from post-death to pre-death is a strong, non-obvious insight with a literal December launch window. Unit economics and scale path are unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Parent consent, cultural taboo and untested Kenyan legal structure; one-season December window.
judges.note: Memorable inversion with a literal December launch window, but parent-alone consent, capacity evidence and counsel clearance make it heavy for a scrappy team.

judges.fatal_flaw: Parent consent, death-talk taboo, undue-influence liability; tiny revenue.
judges.note: Genuinely inverted: convene heirs while the parent is alive, using the December window. Highly original but culturally risky, and the Kenyan legal path is unvalidated.

title: Verified AI Coverage Levels for Vendor Contracts
one_liner: Invert the parent by checking the vendor's insurance from the counterparty's side. AI-enabled vendors upload their policies and get an independent, shareable 'AI Coverage Level' (L0-L3) with monitoring, so enterprise procurement teams can write 'L2 or higher' into contracts. Over time that makes it the insurance-sufficiency standard for AI vendors.
lineage: mutation of I1133 ('Renewal Radar for Silent AI Exclusions'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Proving AI controls and human review to insurers, auditors and clients

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs procurement adoption first; AI-exclusion wave may fade or be bought back.
judges.note: Inverts the buyer chain: counterparties' contracts force vendors to verify. SOC2-style standard for insurance sufficiency, with a Jan 2027 renewal trigger and a vendor-pays motive.

judges.fatal_flaw: No buyer yet writes 'L2 or higher'; attestor lacks standing.
judges.note: Standard-setting play with chicken-and-egg adoption; AI-compliance genre is crowded and vendors rarely pay before a blocked deal.

judges.fatal_flaw: Standard needs buyers to demand it; chicken-and-egg, procurement rarely asks today.
judges.note: Inverted buyer chain is clever, but credentials need adoption before revenue. Near AI-assurance and trust-center crowding. Hard to sell in six months.

title: Orphan Fleet Depot for Bankrupt-Maker Electric Buses
one_liner: Sustainment-as-a-service for school districts and transit agencies stuck with electric buses whose manufacturer went bankrupt, using the military's orphan-platform playbook (salvaged parts pool, configuration control, depot repair, availability guarantees).
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Customers stranded when a product's maker disappears

judges.fatal_flaw: Small orphan base; battery fire liability; parts and tooling likely already liquidated.
judges.note: Military orphan-platform playbook is non-obvious, but small installed base, capital-heavy depot and safety exposure are hard for a scrappy team.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small buyer base, slow public budgets, battery fire liability; Lion's parts estate likely already sold.
judges.note: Acute stranded-bus pain, but tiny buyer pool, slow public procurement, and reverse-engineering battery systems carries fire liability; estate parts may be gone.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small buyer pool; battery repair fire liability; estate parts may already be sold.
judges.note: Military orphan-platform sustainment imported to failed EV makers is a fresh insight. Pooled spares math is real, and every EV bankruptcy widens the base.

title: Outsourced Large-Load Intake Desk for Co-op Pools
one_liner: A stage-gated, applicant-paid intake administrator and cross-utility duplicate registry for G&T co-op pools outside ERCOT, so 5-person planning staffs only ever see evidence-backed projects.
lineage: mutation of I0079 ('Phantom Load Vetting Desk for Rural Utilities'), type: sharpened
cluster: Localities, utilities and landowners facing speculative data-center demand

judges.fatal_flaw: Tariff collateral rules make applicants self-prove; tiny buyer set, slow board adoption.
judges.note: Its own critique concedes fees and deposits substitute for vetting; G&T co-ops are few and slow, so prize looks small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer set; tariffs and collateral rules make applicants self-prove, shrinking the desk's role.
judges.note: Applicant-paid gates and parcel-keyed duplicate registry are sharper than the original, but co-op G&T market is small and regulators are eating the problem.

judges.fatal_flaw: G&T boards and regulators must approve billing applicants; sales cycles exceed six months.
judges.note: Real planner-hours pain; parcel/substation registry is a genuine asset. But co-op boards must approve applicant billing: slow cycles, few customers.

title: Record-on-Request Desk for Superior Courts
one_liner: A managed compliance service that lets a superior court answer any indigent litigant's request for a verbatim record with one certified record per request, priced per record delivered and using the cheapest lawful method, whether steno or electronic recording.
lineage: mutation of I0248 ('Fifteen-Minute Court Reporting for Family Law Hearings'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Small litigation practices lacking evidence, records and benchmark tools

judges.fatal_flaw: California-only court procurement, ruling-dependent demand, reporter-union opposition; courts may build intake in-house.
judges.note: Fixes the parent's illegal remote-reporting mechanic and outcome pricing is clever, but it is a narrow, slow government services bet on one ruling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Court procurement is slow; the steno supply pool it depends on is already short.
judges.note: Fixes parent's illegal remote mechanic and ties to a statutory duty. But it is a 30-40% margin middleman selling to slow, union-sensitive courts.

judges.fatal_flaw: Single-state government buyer; a Judicial Council master agreement could commoditize it.
judges.note: Urgent compliance trigger and outcome pricing help, but it is margin-thin services sold to slow courts, with incumbents able to sell directly.

title: Pet Claims Clearinghouse Starting at the Front Desk
one_liner: Invert the parent: instead of insurers policing vet invoices after the fact, give vet clinics a carrier-agnostic estimate-to-payout tool at the counter, then grow it into the standard transaction layer for pet insurance and a same-day payment network.
lineage: mutation of I1056 ('Unbundling Edits for Pet Insurance Claims'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Pet owners and insurers squeezed by rising vet bills

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers have little reason to adopt a third-party transaction standard; PMS vendors own front desk.
judges.note: Large prize; owning the vet estimate screen across carriers is the real wedge. Risk is PMS vendors and Trupanion bundling it first.

judges.fatal_flaw: Payout predictions need insurer data; PMS vendors and Trupanion can erase the wedge.
judges.note: Counter-side pain is real and $199/month is sellable. But payout prediction lacks insurer data, PMS vendors can integrate, and the network phases need capital.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs carrier cooperation; PMS vendors and Trupanion can replicate the front-desk tool.
judges.note: Provider-side estimate tool fits the demand shown by VetDirect. 'Standard transaction layer' is a meta-pitch with weak defensibility against practice-software vendors.

title: Refund-Netted Dating: Wholesalers Fund the Float
one_liner: Sell regional wholesalers and buying groups a claim-underwritten '28-day MFP dating' program that defers payment on MFP-drug invoice lines and nets them against the refund, so the pharmacy never borrows and the wholesaler is paid a dilution-risk fee to us.
lineage: mutation of I0499 ('Bridge Loans for Medicare Drug-Price Refunds'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Independent pharmacies squeezed by PBMs, refund floats and deserts

judges.fatal_flaw: Few regional wholesalers; Big 3 can build it; guarantee needs insurance licensing.
judges.note: Selling underwriting to the party owning the rails is smart, but the customer set is small and weaker than the lender-neutral bureau version.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs risk capital or licensed carrier; wholesalers control payment path; slow integrations.
judges.note: Smart reframe of wholesaler as best-placed capital, but few regional wholesalers, long sales cycles, and MFP policy is a moving target.

judges.fatal_flaw: Big 3 wholesalers hold the rails; regionals are small; policy may fix the float.
judges.note: Selling dilution underwriting to the rails owner is a smart inversion of the parent lending idea. Window is short and the guarantee needs capital.

title: Graduate Pay Ledger for CDL Schools and Carriers
one_liner: CDL schools get the verified placement and earnings evidence Workforce Pell requires by having graduates upload settlement stubs to a pay-verification app. Carriers pay to reach those graduates with verified pay pages, and lenders pay for stub-based income packets.
lineage: hybrid of I0916 + I0227 (Placement Proof for Workforce Pell Providers + Verified Pay Receipts for Truck Driver Hiring). Why stronger: Placement Proof alone has to chase completers by text and email, and the pay app alone has a slow consumer cold start. Combined, schools deliver a captive, motivated cohort of new drivers every month, the pay data comes from the exact graduates schools need to verify, and carriers and lenders subsidize a verification service that schools would otherwise pay for entirely themselves.
cluster: Colleges and training programs under new federal loan caps and earnings tests

judges.fatal_flaw: States may verify placement from wage records; SIS vendors can bolt it on.
judges.note: Hybrid fixes pay-app cold start with a compliance-driven school wedge, but the market is small, three-sided, and driver stub uploads will lag.

judges.fatal_flaw: State wage records could verify placement; SIS vendors can bolt it on.
judges.note: Hybrid truly fixes the pay app's cold start with a captive cohort and a compliance deadline. Per-completer revenue is small and the rule is unsettled.

judges.fatal_flaw: Three-sided cold start; Pell rules may accept state wage records instead.
judges.note: Hybrid is bigger, not stronger: graduates must upload stubs, carriers and lenders must pay; school compliance need may be met by wage data.

title: Materials-Leakage Diligence for Trade-Shop Acquirers
one_liner: Sell search-fund, independent-sponsor and roll-up buyers of plumbing/HVAC shops a five-day report that reconciles the target's supplier spend to its customer invoices, sizes the fixable leak as EBITDA, and sets the baseline for a post-close capture program.
lineage: mutation of I0068 ('Contingency Audit of Unbilled Plumbing Materials'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Small trade and service firms underpricing and leaking margin

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny deal volume at $7.5k per report; revenue ceiling in low millions
judges.note: Buyer-pays reframing fixes attribution and willingness to pay, but a few hundred search-fund deals at $7.5k caps revenue far below venture scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: QoE boutiques can add materials reconciliation; small deal volume caps the prize.
judges.note: Changing payer to acquirers fixes the parent's flaws and sells fast, but it is a thin copyable diligence add-on with a small market.

judges.fatal_flaw: Supplier invoice access before LOI is hard; per-deal frequency caps repeat volume.
judges.note: Buyer-pays reframing fixes parent's attribution and willingness-to-pay flaws; tight search-fund communities spread word. Seller data access and QoE overlap are the risks.

title: Warranty Desk Embedded in Maintenance Software
one_liner: A white-label, success-fee warranty desk sold through mid-tier maintenance-tracking and MRO software vendors. The removal event, the PO and the repair invoice meet inside a system the operator already uses, and the software vendor earns a revenue share.
lineage: mutation of I0195 ('Contingency Recovery of Missed Rotable Repair Warranties'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Warranty claims left unfiled

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny niche; power-by-the-hour contracts remove warranty exposure; depends on vendor partnerships.
judges.note: Vendor channel solves data access, and the adoption-not-feature framing is fair. Competitor evidence thin, market small, and a vendor revenue share complicates control.

judges.fatal_flaw: Vendor partnership cycles are slow; power-by-the-hour removes warranty exposure; small market.
judges.note: Channel via maintenance-software vendors fixes data access but adds dependency and a 30% share. A marginal improvement on a tiny niche.

judges.fatal_flaw: Channel dependence; thin small-fleet warranty dollars; power-by-the-hour removes claims.
judges.note: Contingency via maintenance-software vendors is clever distribution, but needs aviation expertise, partner business development, and per-operator recoveries look small.

title: Notarized Mitigation Records: The Evidence Standard for Wildfire Credits
one_liner: A score-agnostic verification layer where contractors capture signed photos that are cross-checked against imagery and issued as portable machine-readable Verified Mitigation Records, which carriers and certifiers accept.
lineage: mutation of I1148 ('Parcel-Level Rebuttals to Wildfire Insurance Scores'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Homeowners and communities losing property insurance in high-risk areas

judges.fatal_flaw: No carrier is obliged to accept the record; three-sided cold start.
judges.note: Signed capture plus imagery cross-check suits the fake-photo era, but the California premise is broken and carriers hold the keys.

judges.fatal_flaw: No payer until carriers accept the record; contractors will not pay for unaccepted proof.
judges.note: Signed-capture provenance is a sound idea, but standard-setting chicken-and-egg with carriers; free pilots do not prove willingness to pay.

judges.fatal_flaw: Carriers need not accept the format; standards need carrier adoption before contractors see value.
judges.note: Signed-capture provenance for mitigation evidence fits the AI-faked-photo era, but it's a standards play with chicken-and-egg adoption and thin per-job revenue.

title: Supplier Watch: Customs Trails Plus Tool Census
one_liner: A supplier-monitoring subscription that reads US customs records for what your factory really ships and to whom, and upgrades to laser-tagged tool census and cavity-fingerprint forensics when the trail looks wrong or a divorce is coming.
lineage: hybrid of I0552 + I1209 (Supplier Divorce Protection: Tool Census and Overrun Forensics + Real-Factory Credentials From Customs Shipping Records). Why stronger: Tool Census alone is a high-ticket, low-frequency service with a long sales cycle, and customs credentials alone compete directly with ImportGenius, Panjiva and ImportYeti. Together, the cheap subscription is the funnel to the expensive census, the census and forensics supply ground truth that makes the credential defensible, and forensic cases keep improving the anomaly model.
cluster: US machine shops and reshoring manufacturers

judges.fatal_flaw: Hybrid sprawls across four products; customs rows often name forwarders, not factories.
judges.note: $2,500 remote audit is an easy first sale into a real fear, but hybrid sprawls, ImportGenius sits adjacent, and China enforcement is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Weak legal value without enforceable IP; cheap tier crowded by ImportGenius.
judges.note: Customs-trail forensics for off-book tooling overruns is useful, but ImportGenius occupies the cheap tier and evidence matters only when IP is enforceable in China.

judges.fatal_flaw: ImportGenius-class tools already sell the subscription; census is slow service work.
judges.note: Customs trail as a remote forensics funnel is clever and sells quickly at $2.5K. Weak legal usefulness for generic parts, and low defensibility.

title: Hours Exchange: Supply Side of the Work Requirement
one_liner: Invert the wallet: instead of helping people prove hours they already work, build the network of pre-certified nonprofit and public hosts that supply verifiable, flexible community-service and training hours, with insured hosts and signed hour records, paid per active member-month by health systems and plans.
lineage: mutation of I0573 ('Medicaid Hours Wallet for Gig Workers'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Benefit-rule changes: Medicaid work rules, SNAP and ACA cliffs

judges.fatal_flaw: Depends on states accepting registry hours; marketplace cold start both sides.
judges.note: Large social prize but needs state acceptance, supply-side network, insurance and workfare-optics management; payers uncertain.

judges.fatal_flaw: Residual no-hours slice is small; state acceptance of host registry unproven; workfare optics.
judges.note: Supply-side inversion is clever and timed to Jan 2027. But the real loss is paperwork, not missing hours; the self-estimated ceiling is small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Unproven payer; most coverage loss is paperwork, not a shortage of hours.
judges.note: Supply-side inversion is interesting and timely for Jan 2027. But the residual slice is small, state acceptance gates everything, and workfare optics hurt.

title: Contributor-Only Delay Outcome Ledger for Immigration Solos
one_liner: A give-to-get ledger that joins public dockets with the USCIS action dates only the filing lawyer sees, sold as a triage score plus a consent-order-first filing pack for a solo's existing stuck files in the four highest-moot districts.
lineage: mutation of I1062 ('Delay-Suit Rails for Stuck Immigration Cases'), type: sharpened
cluster: Immigrant households and workers: status deadlines and paperwork

judges.fatal_flaw: Four-district solo market is tiny; policy shifts could end the delay-suit boom.
judges.note: Contributor-only action-date data is a genuine cornered resource and the triage framing fixes the parent, but the immigration solo market tops out near $1M ARR.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny solo-lawyer market; contributor-only data cold-starts; free guides and boutique templates substitute.
judges.note: Real stuck-file pain, easy upsell to existing clients; ledger is the interesting piece. Small solo market, and moat depends on contributor cold start.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny solo market; contributor ledger cold start; thin docket-data moat.
judges.note: Only the filing lawyer holds USCIS action dates, a real cornered-data insight. But the niche is small and boutiques can undercut.

title: Insurer-Paid Total-Loss Add-On Refund Concierge
one_liner: When a financed car is totaled, the auto insurer's settlement packet is exactly what GAP and service-contract administrators demand, so the insurer pays a flat fee to have every unearned add-on refund and GAP claim filed and tracked for the claimant, who keeps 100 percent of the money.
lineage: mutation of I0109 ('Payoff-Triggered Refund Recovery for Credit Unions'), type: new-customer-or-model
cluster: Unclaimed money: settlements, refunds, penalties and unpaid invoices

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurer retention ROI unproven; about $45 per claim caps revenue per carrier.
judges.note: Insurer-pays framing fixes fee optics and lender integration, but $45 per claim and unproven retention ROI make a small, slow-to-sell prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers lack budget motive for claimant refunds; slow carrier sales; consumer refund services exist.
judges.note: Insurer paper unlocks stalled add-on refunds, a decent retention story. Claims-tech vendors can absorb it, and the payer is paying for someone else's money.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers get no loss-ratio benefit; $45 per case is too thin for slow insurer sales.
judges.note: Clever claimant-friendly angle, but retention value is hard to budget. Regional insurers move slowly and revenue per carrier is tiny.

title: Parcel-Level Rebuttals to Wildfire Insurance Scores
one_liner: Evidence packs showing a coarse satellite-derived wildfire score is wrong about one specific lot, filed under new statutory appeal rights.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Homeowners and communities losing property insurance in high-risk areas

judges.fatal_flaw: Nothing compels insurers to accept third-party imagery; California appeal right appears not enacted.
judges.note: Real nonrenewal pain and reachable agents, but acceptance by insurers is uncertain, $99 substitutes cap price, and only Colorado's regime is confirmed.

judges.fatal_flaw: California appeal right appears not enacted; Colorado law may not require insurers to accept imagery.
judges.note: Real 30 m vs 30 cm resolution insight, but only Colorado confirmed, free kits cap price, imagery vendors hold same data.

judges.fatal_flaw: CA appeal right unverified; Colorado law doesn't compel insurers to accept third-party imagery.
judges.note: Clever imagery-versus-30m-score gap, but only Colorado is confirmed, free kits cap price, and a mitigation discount can moot the correction.

title: Load Recovery for Municipal Utilities and Co-ops
one_liner: Sell the verified dead-plant record to the municipal electric utilities and rural co-ops that lose money every month the anchor plant sits dark, priced as a package plus a bonus tied to the load they get back.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lender has no incentive; success fee on member refund is bad optics.
judges.note: Credit union gets no economic benefit from member refunds, success-fee optics are poor, sales cycle is slow, and the SB 766 citation failed to verify.

judges.fatal_flaw: Credit union gets no economic benefit; slow vendor diligence; bad statute citation.
judges.note: Fee optics on member refunds and goodwill-only incentive, plus long core integration cycles; its own mutations fix these problems better.

title: Shared-Aide Pods for 55+ Apartment Buildings
one_liner: One on-site aide team serves 6-10 residents in the same building, delivering assisted-living-style help at a fraction of 1:1 home-care cost.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Home and residential care: labor supply, family caregivers and small-scale models

judges.fatal_flaw: Unit economics break-even at best; licensing makes assisted-living-without-license fragile.
judges.note: Density pricing insight is real and the prize is large. The idea's own numbers do not close, and licensing and care operations are heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Two aides per shift cost more than 6-10 residents can pay.
judges.note: Unit economics break at stated density, licensing is fragile, and senior-care is a predictable pitch with incumbents ready to copy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Own numbers show cost of $4-5k per resident exceeds the $1.8-3.5k price.
judges.note: Unit economics break at 6-15 residents per two-aide shift, and licensing is fragile where service bundles resemble assisted living. Aging-in-place is a crowded thesis.

title: Fifteen-Minute Court Reporting for Family Law Hearings
one_liner: Remove the half-day minimum by dispatching remote stenographers into many short hearings per day, so a family-law litigant gets a certified record of a 15-minute hearing for about $100.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Small litigation practices lacking evidence, records and benchmark tools

judges.fatal_flaw: Gov. Code 69959 bars remote reporting of court records
judges.note: Utilization insight is good, but core mechanic of private remote reporters in California courts is barred by statute; physical-hopping fallback is narrow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Remote court reporting by private reporters is barred by California Gov. Code 69959.
judges.note: Utilization insight is good but the core mechanic is illegal in California courts; the Record-on-Request offspring replaces it.

judges.fatal_flaw: California law bars remote court reporting for private reporters dialing in.
judges.note: Core mechanic is illegal in the target regime. Remaining wedge is narrow physical hopping, and unions are a headwind.

title: GLP-1 Palate Panel for Food R&D
one_liner: A managed panel of GLP-1 users and their households that food and restaurant companies rent to test products, portions and health claims.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Businesses adapting to GLP-1 users' changed consumption

judges.fatal_flaw: Any panel vendor can add a GLP-1 screener; thin-margin research services.
judges.note: Riding the GLP-1 consensus with a research panel. Segmentation insight is fine, but it is project-based services with no durable moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: No moat: sensory CROs and panel vendors can add a GLP-1 segment quickly.
judges.note: Real reformulation wave, but panel recruiting is a grind, CPG sales are slow, and any sensory CRO can add a GLP-1 screener.

judges.fatal_flaw: Panel vendors and sensory CROs can screen GLP-1 users easily.
judges.note: GLP-1 reformulation is the most-discussed food trend. The panel itself is market research with low defensibility, even if the segments are real.

title: Courtroom ETA: Call-Time Network for Family Court
one_liner: A 'FlightAware for family court calendars' that texts litigants, lawyers and freelance reporters and interpreters their predicted call time, giving the queue away and selling the same feed to the professionals who lose half-day minimums waiting.
lineage: mutation of I0248 ('Fifteen-Minute Court Reporting for Family Law Hearings'), type: 10x-or-inverted
cluster: Small litigation practices lacking evidence, records and benchmark tools

judges.fatal_flaw: Free litigant side pays nothing; paid side tiny; needs courthouse density and check-ins.
judges.note: Smart inversion, but main users pay nothing, paying reporters are few, crowd-sourced ETA needs courthouse density, and phone limits and grant-funded sponsors slow everything.

judges.fatal_flaw: No initial payer; two-sided cold start; courts may restrict phone check-ins.
judges.note: FlightAware-for-courts is memorable but the free side pays nothing and the paying reporters are a tiny cohort. Needs dense crowd data before any revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Courtroom phone limits and no clear payer beyond a tiny professional niche.
judges.note: FlightAware-for-courts is cute with real local network effects, but monetization depends on few reporters and slow courts.

title: Family Bank: Bank of Mom and Dad, Papered
one_liner: A family office's real job is governance and records, not investing; for $20/mo, give ordinary parents and adult children a promissory-note, autopay and sibling-fairness ledger for the money that already flows between them.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Making family estate plans fair and contest-proof

judges.fatal_flaw: LoanBack owns documents at $15-30; consumers rarely pay $20/mo.
judges.note: Sibling advancement ledger is a genuine insight, but it is a consumer feature with weak willingness to pay and costly acquisition.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low-frequency consumer use at $20/mo; autopay raises money-transmission questions.
judges.note: Sibling ledger is a genuine insight, but LoanBack owns the document layer and consumer acquisition for a rare event is expensive.

judges.fatal_flaw: LoanBack plus free templates; consumer CAC far exceeds $20/mo value.
judges.note: Sibling ledger is a nice insight, but this is consumer personal-finance tooling with weak willingness to pay and an existing $15-30 competitor.

title: Nonrenewal Cure: Rebutting Insurer Cancellations
one_liner: Nonrenewal notices often cite fixable issues like roof condition, tree overhang or debris. Sell homeowners a fast diagnosis, repair and evidence packet to get re-underwritten instead of dumped on a FAIR plan.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Homeowners and communities losing property insurance in high-risk areas

judges.fatal_flaw: CA SB 1301 commoditizes diagnosis; many flags not curable; insurance licensing exposure.
judges.note: Consumer acquisition against free regulator help and thin referral margins; fixable-notice niche too small to build on.

judges.fatal_flaw: CA SB 1301 commoditizes diagnosis; contractor lead-gen margins thin; likely licensing issues.
judges.note: Consumer-facing contractor referral with a diagnosis hook. Crowded free resources, many flags aren't curable, and the law erodes the paid step.

judges.fatal_flaw: SB 1301 mandates free remediation explanations; contractor lead-gen margins thin.
judges.note: Consumer-facing contractor-dispatch lead-gen with an eroding diagnostic. Many nonrenewals are not cheaply curable, and legal changes commoditize the paid step.

title: ITAR-Safe Identity for New-Space Startups
one_liner: An identity layer that proves a new hire is real, where they actually are and whether they may legally see spacecraft technical data, then feeds that attribute straight into SSO and PLM access controls.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: New defense and drone suppliers: compliance and financing hurdles

judges.fatal_flaw: CMMC Phase 2 suspended, killing why-now; IDV crowded; citizenship-discrimination legal risk.
judges.note: Identity and compliance pattern with a broken timing hook. Okta group flags are easy to DIY, and Persona and archTIS sit adjacent.

judges.fatal_flaw: CMMC why-now collapsed; citizenship-discrimination risk; DIY via Okta group.
judges.note: Identity plus compliance for a niche is a familiar pattern. DoD suspended the Phase 2 cliff, legal exposure under INA 274B, and an IT admin can replicate the core attribute.

judges.fatal_flaw: CMMC Phase 2 suspended; citizenship-check discrimination risk (INA 274B) and trivial DIY substitute.
judges.note: Why-now collapsed: CMMC Phase 2 suspended. Legal exposure on citizenship checks, DIY Okta flag, and crowded compliance and IDV vendors leave a thin paid wedge.

title: Search-Fund Accelerator for Buying Scrap Yards
one_liner: A cohort program that turns laid-off mid-career managers into owner-operators of small scrap yards, e-scrap shops and transfer stations. It brings deal sourcing, environmental diligence and SBA-lender access.
lineage: original (tournament survivor)
cluster: Trade-shop succession and buyouts

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded ETA education market; BIS rule narrow; broker licensing and fee optics.
judges.note: Another buy-boring-businesses cohort aimed at laid-off managers, competing with Codie Sanchez, Kingsway and universities. Tuition and equity model is weak and the BIS premise is overstated.

judges.fatal_flaw: Success depends on closing hard scrap-yard deals; crowded ETA education market.
judges.note: Coaching/cohort plus search-fund education sold to laid-off managers. Yards carry environmental liability, deals take 12+ months, and the BIS rule barely applies.

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded buyer-education market; BIS rule narrow; capital and environmental liability.
judges.note: Search-fund and boring-business roll-up pitch aimed at laid-off managers. The premise is overstated, and buyers face real liability and financing hurdles.

title: Special-Ed Parent Tracker Feeding Host-School Programs
one_liner: A $20-a-month IEP chief of staff for Texas parents whose service-minute logs identify the families and districts where a clinician-led, voucher-funded host-school program is the real solution.
lineage: hybrid of I0289 + I1032 (IEP Chief of Staff for Special-Ed Parents + AltSchool Without Buildings: Disability Programs in Host Schools). Why stronger: The tracker's CAC is subsidized by a payer worth an order of magnitude more per family, and the host program gets pre-qualified, motivated, documented leads instead of buying ads. Shared data tells the business where to open programs. Together it is a full lifecycle (enforce, then exit if enforcement fails) that a competitor with only one half cannot offer.
cluster: K-12 districts' legal service duties: IEPs, attendance, nutrition and Title I

judges.fatal_flaw: Advocate-to-own-program funnel is a conflict of interest; $20 tracker is commodity.
judges.note: IEP Advocate.ai and ChatGPT already cover the tracker; funneling into own voucher-funded school is regulated, hard operating business, not synergy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Advocate-to-placement conflict of interest; accreditation barrier; $20 consumer CAC; IEP Advocate.ai exists.
judges.note: Hybrid stitches a crowded AI IEP tracker to a multi-year school-operator build; steering parents to paid placement taints trust. Not stronger than a single business.

judges.fatal_flaw: TEFA and accreditors may not allow hosted programs; $20 consumer CAC.
judges.note: Core tracker is a cheaper copy of IEP Advocate.ai, host-school half rests on legal gray area, and stacking two businesses adds risk.

title: Rotor Rescue as Scrapyard Deal-Sourcing Engine
one_liner: Use the pay-per-rotor magnet program as the free-to-yard front door that surfaces retiring scrapyard owners and gives search-fund buyers a day-one margin lever and guaranteed magnet supply.
lineage: hybrid of I0626 + I0939 (Search-Fund Accelerator for Buying Scrap Yards + Rotor Rescue: Scrapyard Magnet Pick-and-Pay). Why stronger: The accelerator gets proprietary deal flow and a concrete margin-improvement thesis at day one, which is the hardest thing for a first-time searcher to show a lender or seller. Rotor Rescue gets trusted access to yards, guaranteed volume through acquired yards, and a second revenue line that does not depend on rare-earth prices. Each side removes the other's biggest customer-acquisition cost.
cluster: Trade-shop succession and buyouts

judges.fatal_flaw: Three unrelated customer groups; recyclers can pay yards directly; coaching tuition market is crowded.
judges.note: Stapling a search-fund cohort onto a magnet-pricing service makes it bigger, not stronger. Each half undermines focus and the combined moat is unclear.

judges.fatal_flaw: Four vague customer types; acquiring yards needs capital and operating expertise.
judges.note: Stitches a cohort-tuition search-fund course onto a magnet-pricing program. Not stronger than parts; relies on crowded buyer-education market.

judges.fatal_flaw: Two unrelated businesses glued together; Cyclic can pay yards directly.
judges.note: Hybrid joins a crowded buy-a-boring-business education play with a magnet scheme. The combination is not stronger than either part.
